title: Gapped Quantum Systems: From Higher Dimensional Lieb-Schultz-Mattis to the Quantum Hall Effect
description: Abstract We consider many-body quantum systems on a finite lattice, where the Hilbert space is the tensor product of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces associated with each site, and where the Hamiltonian of the system is a sum of local terms. We are interested in proving uniform bounds on various properties as the size of the lattice tends to infinity.

title: Janus and RG-flow interfaces in three-dimensional gauged supergravity
creator: Kevin Chen, Michael Gutperle, and Charlie Hultgreen-Mena
description: Abstract In this paper, we construct Janus-type solutions of three-dimensional gauged supergravity with sixteen supersymmetries. We find solutions which correspond to interfaces between the same CFT on both sides, as well as RG-flow interfaces between CFTs with different numbers of supersymmetries and central charges.

creator: Venu M. Kalari
description: Abstract The Trifid Nebula is a young, nearby star-forming region where star formation is proposed to have been triggered by cloud-cloud collision (CCC), based on observations of molecular clouds. It offers a unique opportunity to test whether the CCC hypothesis is supported by the spatial distribution and star formation chronology of young stars.

title: Private Interdependent Valuations
creator: Alon Eden, Kira Goldner, Shuran Zheng
description: Abstract We consider the single-item interdependent value setting , where there is a single item sold by a monopolist, n n buyers, and each buyer has a private signal s i s_{i} describing a piece of information about the item.

title: Deep Keyphrase Completion
creator: Yu Zhao, Jia Song, Huali Feng, Fuzhen Zhuang, Qing Li, Xiaojie Wang, Ji Liu
description: Abstract Keyphrase provides accurate information of document content that is highly compact, concise, full of meanings, and widely used for discourse comprehension, organization, and text retrieval. Though previous studies have made substantial efforts for automated keyphrase extraction and generation, surprisingly, few studies have been made for keyphrase completion (KPC). KPC aims to generate more keyphrases for document (e.g.

title: Flows of G 2 -structures on contact Calabi–Yau 7 7 -manifolds
creator: Jason D. Lotay, Henrique N. Sá Earp, Julieth Saavedra
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jason D. Lotay, Henrique N. Sá Earp, Julieth Saavedra. We study the Laplacian flow and coflow on contact Calabi-Yau 7 7 -manifolds. We show that the natural initial condition leads to an ancient solution of the Laplacian flow with a finite time Type I singularity which is not a soliton, whereas it produces an immortal (though neither eternal nor self-similar) solution of the Laplacian coflow which has an infinite time singularity of Type IIb, unless the transverse Calabi–Yau geometry is flat.

creator: \firstname A. \lastname Paliwal \fnsep, \firstname E. \lastname Artis, \firstname W. \lastname Cui, \firstname M. \lastname De Petris, \firstname F.-X. \lastname Désert, \firstname A. \lastname Ferragamo, \firstname G. \lastname Gianfagna, \firstname F. \lastname Kéruzoré, \firstname J.-F. \lastname
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by \firstname A. \lastname Paliwal \fnsep, \firstname E. \lastname Artis, \firstname W. \lastname Cui, \firstname M. \lastname De Petris, \firstname F.-X. \lastname Désert, \firstname A. \lastname Ferragamo, \firstname G. \lastname Gianfagna, \firstname F. \lastname Kéruzoré, \firstname J.-F. \lastname. The simulation database of The Three Hundred Project has been used to pick synthetic clusters of galaxies with properties close to the observational targets of the NIKA2 camera Sunyaev–Zeldovich (SZ) Large Program.

title: Noise and dose reduction in CT brain perfusion acquisition by projecting time attenuation curves onto lower dimensional spaces
creator: Vojtěch Kulvait, Philip Hoelter, Arnd Doerfler, Georg Rose
description: Abstract CT perfusion imaging (CTP) plays an important role in decision making for the treatment of acute ischemic stroke with large vessel occlusion. Since the CT perfusion scan time is approximately one minute, the patient is exposed to a non-negligible dose of ionizing radiation.

title: Resilient Interval Observer for Simultaneous Estimation of States, Modes and Attack Policies Thanks: The authors are with the School for Engineering of Matter, Transport and Energy, Arizona State University, Tempe, AZ, USA (e-mail: mkhajene@asu.edu, zjin43@asu.edu, szyong@asu.edu). This work was sup
creator: Mohammad Khajenejad, Zeyuan Jin, Sze Zheng Yong
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mohammad Khajenejad, Zeyuan Jin, Sze Zheng Yong. This paper considers the problem of designing interval observers for hidden mode switched nonlinear systems with bounded noise signals that are compromised by false data injection and switching attacks.

title: Mass Estimation of Planck Galaxy Clusters using Deep Learning
creator: \firstname Daniel \lastname de Andres \fnsep, \firstname Weiguang \lastname Cui, \firstname Florian \lastname Ruppin, \firstname Marco \lastname De Petris, \firstname Gustavo \lastname Yepes, \firstname Ichraf \lastname Lahouli, \firstname Gianmarco \lastname Aversano, \firstname Romain \lastname Du
description: Abstract Galaxy cluster masses can be inferred indirectly using measurements from X-ray band, Sunyaev-Zeldovich (SZ) effect signal or optical observations. Unfortunately, all of them are affected by some bias. Alternatively, we provide an independent estimation of the cluster masses from the Planck PSZ2 catalog of galaxy clusters using a machine-learning method.

title: Overdensity of SubMillimiter Galaxies in the GJ526 Field mapped with the NIKA2 Camera
creator: \firstname J.-F. \lastname Lestrade \fnsep, \firstname R. \lastname Adam, \firstname P. \lastname Ade, \firstname H. \lastname Ajeddig, \firstname P. \lastname André, \firstname E. \lastname Artis, \firstname H. \lastname Aussel, \firstname A. \lastname Beelen, \firstname A. \lastname Benoît, \first
description: Abstract Using the NIKA2 dual band millimeter camera installed on the IRAM30m telescope, we have mapped a relatively large field ( ∼ 70 \sim 70 arcmin 2 ) in the direction of the star GJ526 to investigate the nature of the sources found with the MAMBO camera at 1.2 mm ten years earlier.

title: Hashtag : Hash Signatures for Online Detection of Fault-Injection Attacks on Deep Neural Networks
creator: Mojan Javaheripi, Farinaz Koushanfar
description: Abstract We propose Hashtag , the first framework that enables high-accuracy detection of fault-injection attacks on Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) with provable bounds on detection performance. Recent literature in fault-injection attacks shows the severe DNN accuracy degradation caused by bit flips.

title: Revisiting spatio-temporal layouts for compositional action recognition
creator: Gorjan Radevski, Marie-Francine Moens, Tinne Tuytelaars
description: Abstract Recognizing human actions is fundamentally a spatio-temporal reasoning problem, and should be, at least to some extent, invariant to the appearance of the human and the objects involved. Motivated by this hypothesis, in this work, we take an object-centric approach to action recognition.

title: Counting Tripods on the Torus Thanks: J.S.A. was partially supported by NSF CAREER grant DMS 1559860 and NSF DMS 2003528 Thanks: D.A. was partially supported by NSF DMS - 1738381 and several PSC-CUNY grants
creator: Jayadev S. Athreya, David Aulicino, Harry Richman
description: Abstract . Motivated by the problem of counting finite BPS webs, we count certain immersed metric graphs, tripods , on the flat torus. Classical Euclidean geometry turns this into a lattice point counting problem in ℂ 2 \mathbb{C}^{2} , and we give an asymptotic counting result using lattice point counting techniques. 1.

title: A subsemigroup of the rook monoid
creator: George Fikioris, Giannis Fikioris
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by George Fikioris, Giannis Fikioris. We define a subsemigroup S n S_{n} of the rook monoid R n R_{n} and investigate its properties. To do this, we represent the nonzero elements of S n S_{n} (which are n × n n\times n matrices) via certain triplets of integers, and develop a closed-form expression representing the product of two elements; these tools facilitate straightforward deductions of a great number of properties.

title: Deep learning for identification and face, gender, expression recognition under constraints
description: Abstract Biometric recognition based on the full face is an extensive research area. However, using only partially visible faces, such as in the case of veiled-persons, is a challenging task. Deep convolutional neural network (CNN) is used in this work to extract the features from veiled-person face images.

title: On a Problem of Steinhaus
creator: Marcin Anholcer, Bartłomiej Bosek, Jarosław Grytczuk, Grzegorz Gutowski, Jakub Przybyło, Rafał Pyzik, Mariusz Zając
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Marcin Anholcer, Bartłomiej Bosek, Jarosław Grytczuk, Grzegorz Gutowski, Jakub Przybyło, Rafał Pyzik, Mariusz Zając. Let N N be a positive integer. A sequence X = ( x 1 , x 2 , … , x N ) X=(x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{N}) of points in the unit interval [ 0 , 1 ) [0,1) is piercing if { x 1 , x 2 , … , x n } ∩ [ i n , i + 1 n ) ≠ ∅ \{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{n}\}\cap\left[\frac{i}{n},\frac{i+1}{n}\right)\neq\emptyset holds for every n = 1

title: Quantum information for a solitonic particle with hyperbolic interaction
creator: A.R.P. Moreira
description: Abstract In this work, we analyze a particle with position-dependent mass, with solitonic mass distribution in a stationary quantum system, for the particular case of the BenDaniel-Duke ordering, in a hyperbolic barrier potential. The kinetic energy ordering of BenDaniel-Duke guarantees the hermiticity of the Hamiltonian operator. We find the analytical solutions of the Schrödinger equation and their respective quantized energies.

title: Implementing a scalable and elastic computing environment based on Cloud Containers
creator: Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659, Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519, Sergio Tasso ORCID:0000-0001-9174-9065, Federico Ragni and, Osvaldo Gervasi ORCID:0000-0003-4327-520X
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659, Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519, Sergio Tasso ORCID:0000-0001-9174-9065, Federico Ragni and, Osvaldo Gervasi ORCID:0000-0003-4327-520X. In this article we look at the potential of cloud containers and we provide some guidelines for companies and organisations that are starting to look at how to migrate their legacy infrastructure to something modern, reliable and scalable. We propose an architecture that has an excellent relationship between the cost of implementation and the benefits it can bring, based on the ”Pilot Light” topology.

title: Teaching Math with the help of Virtual Reality
creator: Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519 Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659 Natale Amato ORCID:0000-0001-5104-9494 Osvaldo Gervasi ORCID:0000-0003-4327-520X
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519 Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659 Natale Amato ORCID:0000-0001-5104-9494 Osvaldo Gervasi ORCID:0000-0003-4327-520X. In the present work we intend to introduce a system based on VR (Virtual Reality) for examining analytical-geometric structures that occur in the study of mathematics and physics concepts in the last high school classes.

title: Hilbert series of Parallelogram Polyominoes Thanks: This work was supported by The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey - TUBITAK (Grant No: 118F169).
creator: Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Giancarlo Rinaldo, Francesco Romeo
description: Abstract . We present a conjecture about the reduced Hilbert series of the coordinate ring of a simple polyomino in terms of particular arrangements of non-attacking rooks that can be placed on the polyomino. By using a computational approach, we prove that the above conjecture holds for all simple polyominoes up to rank 11 11 .

title: A new method for binary classification of proteins with Machine Learning
creator: Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659 Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519 Andrea Lombardi ORCID:0000-0002-7875-2697 Noelia Faginas-Lago ORCID:0000-0002-4056-3364 Osvaldo Gervasi ORCID:0000-0003-4327-520X
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659 Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519 Andrea Lombardi ORCID:0000-0002-7875-2697 Noelia Faginas-Lago ORCID:0000-0002-4056-3364 Osvaldo Gervasi ORCID:0000-0003-4327-520X. In this work we set out to find a method to classify protein structures using a Deep Learning methodology.

title: An immersive Open Source environment using Godot
creator: Francesca Santucci, Federico Frenguelli, Alessandro De Angelis Ilaria Cuccaro Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659 Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519
description: Abstract We present a sample implementation of a Virtual and Augmented Reality immersive environment based on Free and Libre Open Source Hardware and Software and the HTC Vive system, used to enhance the immersive experience of the user and to track her/his movements.

title: Binary classification of proteins by a Machine Learning approach
creator: Damiano Perri ORCID:0000-0001-6815-6659 Marco Simonetti ORCID:0000-0003-2923-5519 Andrea Lombardi ORCID:0000-0002-7875-2697 Noelia Faginas-Lago ORCID:0000-0002-4056-3364 Osvaldo Gervasi ORCID:0000-0003-4327-520X
description: Abstract In this work we present a system based on a Deep Learning approach, by using a Convolutional Neural Network, capable of classifying protein chains of amino acids based on the protein description contained in the Protein Data Bank. Each protein is fully described in its chemical-physical-geometric properties in a file in XML format.

title: The sup-norm problem beyond the newform
creator: Edgar Assing
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Edgar Assing. In this note we take up the classical sup-norm problem for automorphic forms and view it from a new angle. Given a twist minimal automorphic representation π \pi we consider a special small G ​ L 2 ​ ( ℤ p ) GL_{2}(\mathbb{Z}_{p}) -type V V in π \pi and prove global sup-norm bounds for an average over an orthonormal basis of V V . We achieve a non-trivial saving when the dimension of V V grows.

title: An Evaluation of WebAssembly and eBPF as Offloading Mechanisms in the Context of Computational Storage
creator: Wenjun Huang, Marcus Paradies
description: Abstract As the volume of data that needs to be processed continues to increase, we also see renewed interests in near-data processing in the form of computational storage, with eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) being proposed as a vehicle for computation offloading. However, discussions in this regard have so far ignored viable alternatives, and no convincing analysis has been provided.

title: Discrete Bilal distribution with right-censored data
creator: Bruno Caparroz Lopes de Freitas a , Jorge Alberto Achcar b , Marcos Vinicius de Oliveira Peres b , Edson Zangiacomi Martinez b
description: Abstract This paper presents inferences for the discrete Bilal (DB) distribution introduced by Altun et al. (2020). We consider parameter estimation for DB distribution in the presence of randomly right-censored data. We use maximum likelihood and Bayesian methods for the estimation of the model parameters. We also consider the inclusion of a cure fraction in the model.

title: One- and two-qubit gate infidelities due to motional errors in trapped ions and electrons
creator: R. Tyler Sutherland, Qian Yu, Kristin M. Beck, Hartmut Häffner
description: Abstract In this work, we derive analytic formulae that determine the effect of error mechanisms on one- and two-qubit gates in trapped ions and electrons. First, we analyze, and derive expressions for, the effect of driving field inhomogeneities on one-qubit gate fidelities.

title: Tadpole contribution to magnetic photon-graviton conversion
creator: N. Ahmadiniaz, F. Bastianelli, F. Karbstein, C. Schubert
description: Abstract Photon-graviton conversion in a magnetic field is a process that is usually studied at tree level, but the one-loop corrections due to scalars and spinors have also been calculated. Differently from the tree-level process, at one-loop one finds the amplitude to depend on the photon polarization, leading to dichroism.

title: The point spectrum of the Dirac Hamiltonian on the zero-gravity Kerr-Newman spacetime
creator: M. Kiessling, E. Ling, and A. S. Tahvildar-Zadeh
description: Abstract In this short paper, we review the Dirac equation on the zero-gravity Kerr-Newman spacetime. Our main objective is to provide a correspondence between the classification of the bound states for the zGKN spectrum and the usual hydrogenic states 1 ​ s 1 / 2 1s_{1/2} , 2 ​ s 1 / 2 2s_{1/2} , etc. of the Hydrogen atom.

title: Efficacy of the symmetry-adapted basis for ab initio nucleon-nucleus interactions for light- and intermediate-mass nuclei
creator: A. Mercenne, K. D. Launey, T. Dytrych, J. E. Escher, S. Quaglioni, G. H. Sargsyan, J. P. Draayer
description: Abstract We study the efficacy of a new ab initio framework that combines the symmetry-adapted (SA) no-core shell-model approach with the resonating group method (RGM) for unified descriptions of nuclear structure and reactions. We obtain ab initio neutron-nucleus interactions for 4 He, 16 O, and 20 Ne targets, starting with realistic nucleon-nucleon potentials.

title: First and second moments of the size distribution of bond percolation clusters on regular graphs
creator: Nicolas Lanchier, Axel La Salle
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nicolas Lanchier, Axel La Salle. Motivated by network resilience and insurance premiums in the context of cyber security, we derive universal upper bounds for the first and second moments of the size of bond percolation clusters on finite regular graphs. Thinking of the clusters as dynamical objects coupled with branching processes gives a first set of bounds that are accurate when the probability of an edge being open is small.

title: Radio Emission of Pulsars. I. Slow Tearing of a Quantizing Magnetic Field
creator: Christopher Thompson
description: Abstract The pulsed radio emission of rotating neutron stars is connected to slow tearing instabilities feeding off an inhomogeneous twist profile within the open circuit. This paper considers the stability of a weakly sheared, quantizing magnetic field in which the current is supported by a relativistic particle flow.

title: A Strongly-Labelled Polyphonic Dataset of Urban Sounds with Spatiotemporal Context
creator: \authorblockN Kenneth Ooi, Karn N. Watcharasupat, Santi Peksi, Furi Andi Karnapi, Zhen-Ting Ong, Danny Chua, Hui-Wen Leow, Li-Long Kwok, Xin-Lei Ng, Zhen-Ann Loh, and Woon-Seng Gan \authorblockA School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Emails: {woo
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by \authorblockN Kenneth Ooi, Karn N. Watcharasupat, Santi Peksi, Furi Andi Karnapi, Zhen-Ting Ong, Danny Chua, Hui-Wen Leow, Li-Long Kwok, Xin-Lei Ng, Zhen-Ann Loh, and Woon-Seng Gan \authorblockA School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Emails: {woo. This paper introduces SINGA:PURA , a strongly labelled polyphonic urban sound dataset with spatiotemporal context. The data were collected via several recording units deployed across Singapore as a part of a wireless acoustic sensor network.

title: Lattice QED in external electromagnetic fields
creator: J. B. Kogut
description: Abstract We study QED in external electromagnetic fields using methods developed for simulating lattice QCD. Our first project is to simulate QED in a constant (in space and time) external magnetic field on a euclidean space-time lattice using the Rational Hybrid Monte Carlo (RHMC) method.

title: Radio Emission of Pulsars. II. Coherence Catalyzed by Cerenkov-Unstable Shear Alfvén Waves
creator: Christopher Thompson
description: Abstract This paper explores small-scale departures from force-free electrodynamics around a rotating neutron star, extending our treatment of resistive instability in a quantizing magnetic field. A secondary, Cerenkov instability is identified: relativistic particles flowing through thin current sheets excite propagating charge perturbations that are localized near the sheets.

title: Leveraging Advantages of Interactive and Non-Interactive Models for Vector-Based Cross-Lingual Information Retrieval
creator: Linlong Xu, Baosong Yang, Xiaoyu Lv, Tianchi Bi, Dayiheng Liu, Haibo Zhang
description: Abstract Interactive and non-interactive model are the two de-facto standard frameworks in vector-based cross-lingual information retrieval (V-CLIR), which embed queries and documents in synchronous and asynchronous fashions, respectively. From the retrieval accuracy and computational efficiency perspectives, each model has its own superiority and shortcoming. In this paper, we propose a novel framework to leverage the advantages of these two paradigms.

title: Multidimensional Kyle-Back model with a risk averse informed trader Thanks: This version: November 1st, 2021.
creator: Shreya Bose), Ibrahim Ekren
description: Abstract We study the continuous time Kyle-Back model with a risk averse informed trader. We show that in a market with multiple assets and non-Gaussian prices an equilibrium exists. The equilibrium is constructed by considering a Fokker-Planck equation and a system of partial differential equations that are coupled with an optimal transport type constraint at maturity.

title: Arecibo-Green Bank-LOFAR Carbon Radio Recombination Line observations toward cold H i Clouds
creator: D. Anish Roshi, W. M. Peters, K. L. Emig, P. Salas, J. B. R. Oonk, M. E. Lebrón, J. M. Dickey
description: Abstract We present results from a search for radio recombination lines in three H i self-absorbing (HISA) clouds at 750 MHz and 321 MHz with the Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope (GBT), and in three Galactic Plane positions at 327 MHz with the Arecibo Telescope.

title: Directed flow of charged particles within idealized viscous hydrodynamics at energies available at the BNL Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider and at the CERN Large Hadron Collider Preprint: This line only printed with preprint option
creator: Ze-Fang Jiang, C. B. Yang, Qi Peng
description: Abstract Following the Boz e ˙ \dot{\textrm{e}} k-Wyskiel parametrization tilted initial condition, an alternative way to construct a longitudinal tilted fireball based on the Glauber collision geometry is presented. This longitudinal tilted initial condition combined with the Ideal-CLVisc (3 + 1)D hydrodynamic model, a nonvanishing directed flow coefficient v 1 v_{1} in a wide rapidity range is observed.

title: Multi-Glimpse Network: A Robust and Efficient Classification Architecture based on Recurrent Downsampled Attention
creator: Sia Huat Tan, Runpei Dong, Kaisheng Ma
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sia Huat Tan, Runpei Dong, Kaisheng Ma. Most feedforward convolutional neural networks spend roughly the same effort for each pixel. Yet human visual recognition is an interaction between eye movements and spatial attention, which we will have several glimpses of an object in different regions. Inspired by this observation, we propose an end-to-end trainable M ulti- G limpse N etwork ( MGNet ) which aims to tackle the challenges of high computation and the lack of robustness based on recurrent downsampled attention mechanism.

title: Three-boson stability for boosted interactions towards the zero-range limit Journal: Physics Letters B
creator: K. Mohseni, A. J. Chaves, D. R. da Costa, T. Frederico, M. R. Hadizadeh
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by K. Mohseni, A. J. Chaves, D. R. da Costa, T. Frederico, M. R. Hadizadeh. We study the three-boson bound-state mass and wave functions for ground and excited states within the three-body relativistic framework with Kamada and Glöcke boosted potentials in the limit of a zero-range interaction. We adopt a nonrelativistic short-range separable potential, with Yamaguchi and Gaussian form factors, and drive them towards the zero-range limit by letting the form factors’ momentum scales go to large values while keeping the two-body binding fixed.

title: Obvious Manipulability of Voting Rules
creator: Haris Aziz, Alexander Lam
description: Abstract The Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem states that no unanimous and non-dictatorial voting rule is strategyproof. We revisit voting rules and consider a weaker notion of strategyproofness called not obvious manipulability that was proposed by Troyan and Morrill (2020). We identify several classes of voting rules that satisfy this notion.

title: W[1]-hardness of Outer Connected Dominating set in d-degenerate Graphs
creator: Mohsen Alambardar Meybodi
description: Abstract A set D ⊆ V D\subseteq V of a graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) is called an outer-connected dominating set of G G if every vertex v v not in D D is adjacent to at least one vertex in D D , and the induced subgraph of G G on V ∖ D V\setminus

title: Probing to Minimize
creator: Weina Wang ⓡ Anupam Gupta ⓡ Jalani Williams
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Weina Wang ⓡ Anupam Gupta ⓡ Jalani Williams. We develop approximation algorithms for set-selection problems with deterministic constraints, but random objective values, i.e., stochastic probing problems. When the goal is to maximize the objective, approximation algorithms for probing problems are well-studied. On the other hand, few techniques are known for minimizing the objective, especially in the adaptive setting, where information about the random objective is revealed during the set-selection process and allowed to influence it.

title: Recent Advancements in Self-Supervised Paradigms for Visual Feature Representation
creator: Mrinal Anand, Aditya Garg
description: Abstract We witnessed a massive growth in the supervised learning paradigm in the past decade. Supervised learning requires a large amount of labeled data to reach state-of-the-art performance. However, labeling the samples requires a lot of human annotation. To avoid the cost of labeling data, self-supervised methods were proposed to make use of largely available unlabeled data.

title: Building Legal Datasets
creator: Jerrold Soh Tsin Howe
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jerrold Soh Tsin Howe. Data-centric AI calls for better, not just bigger, datasets. As data protection laws with extra-territorial reach proliferate worldwide, ensuring datasets are legal is an increasingly crucial yet overlooked component of “better”. To help dataset builders become more willing and able to navigate this complex legal space, this paper reviews key legal obligations surrounding ML datasets, examines the practical impact of data laws on ML pipelines, and offers a framework for building legal datasets.

title: Deterministic Minimum Cut in Poly-logarithmic Maximum Flows Thanks: A preliminary version of this paper appeared in the Proceedings of the IEEE Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS), 2020.
creator: Jason Li, Debmalya Panigrahi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jason Li, Debmalya Panigrahi. We give a deterministic algorithm for finding the minimum (weight) cut of an undirected graph on n n vertices and m m edges using polylog ​ ( n ) \textup{polylog}(n) calls to any maximum flow subroutine.

title: Determination of the generalized parton distributions through the analysis of the world electron scattering data considering two-photon exchange corrections
creator: Hadi Hashamipour a, Muhammad Goharipour b,a, K. Azizi b,c,a, S.V. Goloskokov d
description: Abstract We determine the valence generalized parton distributions (GPDs) H v q H_{v}^{q} and E v q E_{v}^{q} with their uncertainties at zero skewness by performing a χ 2 \chi^{2} analysis of the world electron scattering data considering two-photon exchange corrections.

title: Scalable mixed-domain Gaussian process modeling and model reduction for longitudinal data
creator: Juho Timonen, Harri Lähdesmäki
description: Abstract Gaussian process (GP) models that combine both categorical and continuous input variables have found use in analysis of longitudinal data and computer experiments. However, standard inference for these models has the typical cubic scaling, and common scalable approximation schemes for GPs cannot be applied since the covariance function is non-continuous.

title: Multiple generalized cluster structures on D ⁡ ( GL n ) D(\GL_{n})
creator: Dmitriy Voloshyn
description: Abstract We produce a large class of generalized cluster structures on the Drinfeld double of GL n \GL_{n} that are compatible with Poisson brackets given by Belavin-Drinfeld classification. The resulting construction is compatible with the previous results on cluster structures on GL n \GL_{n} . 0 0 footnotetext: Published in Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 11 (46) (2023), 1–78. doi: 10.1017/fms.2023.

title: What is chiral susceptibility probing?
creator: K. Suzuki
description: Abstract In the early days of QCD, the axial U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) anomaly was considered as a trigger for the breaking of the S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) L × S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) R SU(2)_{L}\times SU(2)_{R} symmetry through topological excitations of gluon fields.

title: Numerical simulation of self-dual U(1) lattice field theory with electric and magnetic matter Thanks: Based on a parallel talk by M. Anosova.
creator: Maria Anosova, Christof Gattringer, Nabil Iqbal, Tin Sulejmanpasic, Institute of Physics, University of Graz, 8010 Graz, Austria FWF - Austrian Science Fund, 1090 Vienna, Austria Department of Mathematical Sciences, Durham University, Durham DH1 3LE, UK E-mail: E-mail: E-mail: E-mail
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Maria Anosova, Christof Gattringer, Nabil Iqbal, Tin Sulejmanpasic, Institute of Physics, University of Graz, 8010 Graz, Austria FWF - Austrian Science Fund, 1090 Vienna, Austria Department of Mathematical Sciences, Durham University, Durham DH1 3LE, UK E-mail: E-mail: E-mail: E-mail. We study a recently proposed formulation of U(1) lattice field theory with electric and magnetic matter based on the Villain formulation. This discretization allows for a duality that gives rise to relations between weak and strong gauge coupling.

title: Tests of Lorentz Invariance
creator: Jun-Jie Wei and Xue-Feng Wu
description: Abstract Lorentz invariance is a fundamental symmetry of both Einstein’s theory of general relativity and quantum field theory. However, deviations from Lorentz invariance at energies approaching the Planck scale are predicted in many quantum gravity theories seeking to unify the force of gravity with the other three fundamental forces of matter.

title: Privacy-Preserving Energy Storage Sharing with Blockchain and Secure Multi-Party Computation
creator: Nan Wang, Sid Chi-Kin Chau, Yue Zhou
description: Abstract . Energy storage provides an effective way of shifting temporal energy demands and supplies, which enables significant cost reduction under time-of-use energy pricing plans. Despite its promising benefits, the cost of present energy storage remains expensive, presenting a major obstacle to practical deployment.

title: Fair-SSL: Building fair ML Software with less data CCS: Software and its engineering Software creation and management CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning Conference: International Workshop on Equitable Data and Technology; May 9, 2022; Pittsburgh, PA, USA International Workshop on Equitabl
creator: Joymallya Chakraborty, Suvodeep Majumder, Huy Tu
description: Abstract . Ethical bias in machine learning models has become a matter of concern in the software engineering community. Most of the prior software engineering works concentrated on finding ethical bias in models rather than fixing it. After finding bias, the next step is mitigation. Prior researchers mainly tried to use supervised approaches to achieve fairness.

title: Analysis of Deep Ritz Methods for Laplace Equations with Dirichlet Boundary Condition
creator: Chenguang Duan, Yuling Jiao, Yanming Lai, Xiliang Lu, Qimeng Quan, Jerry Zhijian Yang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chenguang Duan, Yuling Jiao, Yanming Lai, Xiliang Lu, Qimeng Quan, Jerry Zhijian Yang. Deep Ritz methods (DRM) have been proven numerically to be efficient in solving partial differential equations. In this paper, we present a convergence rate in H 1 H^{1} norm for deep Ritz methods for Laplace equations with Dirichlet boundary condition, where the error depends on the depth and width in the deep neural networks and the number of samples explicitly.

title: Approximate Gomory–Hu Tree Is Faster Than n − 1 n-1 Max-Flows
creator: Jason Li, Debmalya Panigrahi
description: Abstract The Gomory-Hu tree or cut tree (Gomory and Hu, 1961) is a classic data structure for reporting ( s , t ) (s,t) mincuts (and by duality, the values of ( s , t ) (s,t) maxflows) for all pairs of vertices s s and t t in an undirected graph.

title: Constraining AGN feedback model with SZ profile
creator: \firstname Hideki \lastname Tanimura \fnsep, \firstname Gary \lastname Hinshaw, \firstname Ian G. \lastname McCarthy, \firstname Ludovic \lastname Van Waerbeke, \firstname Nabila \lastname Aghanim \firstname Yin-Zhe \lastname Ma, \firstname Alexander \lastname Mead, \firstname Tilman \lastname Tröst
description: Abstract Relativistic jets from AGN have a wide range of impacts on galaxy groups and clusters and are key for understanding their formation and physical properties. However, this non-gravitational process is not well understood. Galaxy groups with shallow gravitational potentials are ideal laboratories to study and constrain the AGN feedback model.

title: Salt-based autopeering for DLT-networks
creator: Sebastian Müller 1 2 , Angelo Capossele 2 , Bartosz Kuśmierz 2 , Vivian Lin 2 , Hans Moog 2 , Andreas Penzkofer 2 , Olivia Saa 2 , William Sanders 2 , Wolfgang Welz 2
description: Abstract The security of any Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) depends on the safety of the network layer. Much effort has been put into understanding the consensus layer of DLTs. However, many network layer designs seem ad-hoc and lack a careful analysis of the influence of the design decisions on the whole DLT system.

title: Testing macroecological theories in cryptocurrency market: neutral models can not describe diversity patterns and their variation
creator: Edgardo Brigatti, Estevan Augusto Amazonas Mendes
description: Abstract We develop an analysis of the cryptocurrency market borrowing methods and concepts from ecology. This approach makes it possible to identify specific diversity patterns and their variation, in close analogy with ecological systems, and to characterize the cryptocurrency market in an effective way.

title: Antenna De-Embedding in FDTD Using Spherical Wave Functions by Exploiting Orthogonality
creator: Leonardo Mörlein 1 , Lukas Berkelmann 1 , Dirk Manteuffel 1
description: Abstract De-embedding antennas from the channel using Spherical Wave Functions (SWF) is a useful method to reduce the numerical effort in the simulation of wearable antennas. In this paper an analytical solution to the De-embedding problem is presented in form of surface integrals.

title: Molecular Bond Engineering and Feature Learning for the Design of Hybrid Organic-Inorganic Perovskites Solar Cells with Strong Non-Covalent Halogen-Cation Interactions
creator: Johannes L. Teunissen, Fabiana Da Pieve
description: Abstract Hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites are exceedingly interesting candidates for new solar energy technologies, for both ground-based and space applications. However, their large-scale production is hampered by the lack of long-term stability, mostly associated to ion migration. The specific role of non-covalent bonds in contributing to the stability remains elusive, and in certain cases controversial.

title: L 2 L^{2} -blowup estimates of the wave equation and its application to local energy decay
creator: Ryo Ikehata
description: Abstract We consider the Cauchy problems in 𝐑 n {\bf R}^{n} for the wave equation with a weighted L 1 L^{1} -initial data. We derive sharp infinite time blowup estimates of the L 2 L^{2} -norm of solutions in the case of n = 1 n=1 and n = 2 n=2 .

title: Sizable Time-reversal Violating Effects in Bottom Baryon Decays
creator: Chia-Wei Liu and Chao-Qiang Geng
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chia-Wei Liu and Chao-Qiang Geng. We study time-reversal (T) asymmetries in the charmless two-body decays of antitriplet bottom baryons. We find that in 𝐁 b → 𝐁 n ​ P {\bf B}_{b}\to{\bf B}_{n}P with 𝐁 b = ( Ξ b − , Ξ b 0 , Λ b ) {\bf B}_{b}=(\Xi_{b}^{-},\,\Xi_{b}^{0},\,\Lambda_{b}) and 𝐁 n ​ ( P ) {\bf B}_{n}(P) a octet baryon (pseudoscalar meson), the positive and negative helicity amplitudes are both sizable, resulting in the large T-violating effects.

title: LAION-400M: Open Dataset of CLIP-Filtered 400 Million Image-Text Pairs
creator: Christoph Schuhmann, Richard Vencu, Romain Beaumont, Robert Kaczmarczyk, Clayton Mullis, Aarush Katta, Theo Coombes, Jenia Jitsev, Aran Komatsuzaki
description: Abstract Multi-modal language-vision models trained on hundreds of millions of image-text pairs (e.g. CLIP, DALL-E) gained a recent surge, showing remarkable capability to perform zero- or few-shot learning and transfer even in absence of per-sample labels on target image data.

title: Efficient algorithms for optimization problems involving semi-algebraic range searching
creator: Matthew J. Katz, Micha Sharir
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Matthew J. Katz, Micha Sharir. We present a general technique, based on parametric search with some twist, for solving a variety of optimization problems on a set of semi-algebraic geometric objects of constant complexity.

title: Load Restoration in Islanded Microgrids: Formulation and Solution Strategies
creator: Shourya Bose, Yu Zhang
description: Abstract Adverse circumstances such as extreme weather events can cause significant disruptions to normal operation of electric distribution systems (DS), which includes isolating parts of the DS due to damaged transmission equipment. In this paper, we consider the problem of load restoration in a microgrid (MG) that is islanded from the upstream DS.

title: Automatic Evaluation and Moderation of Open-domain Dialogue Systems
creator: Chen Zhang, João Sedoc, Luis Fernando D’Haro, Rafael Banchs, Alexander Rudnicky
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chen Zhang, João Sedoc, Luis Fernando D’Haro, Rafael Banchs, Alexander Rudnicky. The development of Open-Domain Dialogue Systems (ODS) is a trending topic due to the large number of research challenges, large societal and business impact, and advances in the underlying technology.

title: Lingua Custodia’s participation at the WMT 2021 Machine Translation using Terminologies shared task
creator: Melissa Ailem, Jinghsu Liu, Raheel Qader
description: Abstract This paper describes Lingua Custodia’s submission to the WMT21 shared task on machine translation using terminologies. We consider three directions, namely English to French, Russian, and Chinese. We rely on a Transformer-based architecture as a building block, and we explore a method which introduces two main changes to the standard procedure to handle terminologies.

title: Conditional Graph Attention Networks for Distilling and Refining Knowledge Graphs in Recommendation Conference: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; November 1–5, 2021; Virtual Event, Australia. Proceedings of the 30th ACM Int’l Conf. on Infor
creator: Ke Tu, Peng Cui, Daixin Wang, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou, Yuan Qi, Wenwu Zhu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ke Tu, Peng Cui, Daixin Wang, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou, Yuan Qi, Wenwu Zhu. Knowledge graph is generally incorporated into recommender systems to improve overall performance. Due to the generalization and scale of the knowledge graph, most knowledge relationships are not helpful for a target user-item prediction. To exploit the knowledge graph to capture target-specific knowledge relationships in recommender systems, we need to distill the knowledge graph to reserve the useful information and refine the knowledge to capture the users’ preferences.

title: Spatiotemporal Weather Data Predictions with Shortcut Recurrent-Convolutional Networks: A Solution for the Weather4cast challenge
creator: Jussi Leinonen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jussi Leinonen. This paper presents the neural network model that was used by the author in the Weather4cast 2021 Challenge Stage 1, where the objective was to predict the time evolution of satellite-based weather data images. The network is based on an encoder-forecaster architecture making use of gated recurrent units (GRU), residual blocks and a contracting/expanding architecture with shortcuts similar to U-Net. A GRU variant utilizing residual blocks in place of convolutions is also introduced.

title: Testing the monocentric standard urban model in a global sample of cities
creator: Charlotte Liotta, Vincent Viguié, Quentin Lepetit
description: Abstract Using a unique dataset containing gridded data on population densities, rents, housing sizes, and transportation in 192 cities worldwide, we investigate the empirical relevance of the monocentric standard urban model (SUM). Overall, the SUM seems surprisingly capable of capturing the inner structure of cities, both in developed and developing countries.

title: Mechanochemical models for calcium waves in embryonic epithelia
creator: Katerina Kaouri, Paul E. Méndez, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier
description: Abstract In embryogenesis, epithelial cells, acting as individual entities or as coordinated aggregates in a tissue, exhibit strong coupling between chemical signalling and mechanical responses to internally or externally applied stresses. Intercellular communication in combination with such coordination of morphogenetic movements can lead to drastic modifications in the calcium distribution in the cells.

title: Mitigating long queues and waiting times with service resetting
creator: Ofek Lauber Bonomo 1 , Arnab Pal 2 and Shlomi Reuveni 1
description: Abstract What determines the average length of a queue which stretches in front of a service station? The answer to this question clearly depends on the average rate at which jobs arrive to the queue and on the average rate of service.

title: Marriage is a Peach and a Chalice: Modelling Cultural Symbolism on the Semantic Web Conference: Proceedings of the 11th Knowledge Capture Conference; December 2–3, 2021; Virtual Event, USA Proceedings of the 11th Knowledge Capture Conference (K-CAP ’21), December 2–3, 2021, Virtual Event, USA Price:
creator: Bruno Sartini, Marieke van Erp, Aldo Gangemi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bruno Sartini, Marieke van Erp, Aldo Gangemi. In this work, we fill the gap in the Semantic Web in the context of Cultural Symbolism. Building upon earlier work in ( Sartini and Gangemi 2021 ) , we introduce the Simulation Ontology, an ontology that models the background knowledge of symbolic meanings, developed by combining the concepts taken from the authoritative theory of Simulacra and Simulations of Jean Baudrillard with symbolic structures and content taken from “Symbolism: a Comprehensive Dictionary” by Steven Olderr.

title: Noise inference for ergodic Lévy driven SDE This work was partly supported by JST CREST Grant Number JPMJCR14D7, Japan.
creator: Hiroki Masuda, Lorenzo Mercuri, Yuma Uehara
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hiroki Masuda, Lorenzo Mercuri, Yuma Uehara. We study inference for the driving Lévy noise of an ergodic stochastic differential equation (SDE) model, when the process is observed at high-frequency and long time and when the drift and scale coefficients contain finite-dimensional unknown parameters.

title: Velocimetry in rapidly rotating convection: spatial correlations, flow structures and length scales
creator: Matteo Madonia, Andrés J. Aguirre Guzmán, Herman J. H. Clercx, Rudie P. J. Kunnen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Matteo Madonia, Andrés J. Aguirre Guzmán, Herman J. H. Clercx, Rudie P. J. Kunnen. Rotating Rayleigh–Bénard convection is an oft-employed model system to evaluate the interplay of buoyant forcing and Coriolis forces due to rotation, an eminently relevant interaction of dynamical effects found in many geophysical and astrophysical flows.

title: Model-Based Episodic Memory Induces Dynamic Hybrid Controls
creator: Hung Le, Thommen Karimpanal George, Majid Abdolshah, Truyen Tran, Svetha Venkatesh
description: Abstract Episodic control enables sample efficiency in reinforcement learning by recalling past experiences from an episodic memory. We propose a new model-based episodic memory of trajectories addressing current limitations of episodic control. Our memory estimates trajectory values, guiding the agent towards good policies.

title: On resistance matrices of weighted balanced digraphs

Then the resistance distance between any two vertices i i and j j is given by r i ​ j := l i ​ i † + l j ​ j † − 2 ​ l i ​ j † r_{ij}:=l_{ii}^{{\dagger}}+l_{jj}^{{\dagger}}-2l_{ij}^{{\dagger}} , where l i ​ j † l_{ij}^{\dagger} is the ( i , j ) th (i,j)^{\rm th} entry

title: General considerations in unbalanced fourth-order interference
creator: Z. Y. Ou, Xiaoying Li
description: Abstract Interferometry has been used widely in sensing application. However, the technique is limited by the finite coherence time of the light sources when the interference paths are not balanced. Higher-order interference effects involve intensity correlations between multiple detectors and may have the advantage over the traditional second order interference effect exhibited in only one detector.

title: Predictive Auto-scaling with OpenStack Monasca Conference: 2021 IEEE/ACM 14th International Conference on Utility and Cloud Computing; December 6–9, 2021; Leicester, United Kingdom 2021 IEEE/ACM 14th International Conference on Utility and Cloud Computing (UCC’21), December 6–9, 2021, Leicester, Uni
creator: Giacomo Lanciano, Filippo Galli, Tommaso Cucinotta, Davide Bacciu, Andrea Passarella
description: Abstract . Cloud auto-scaling mechanisms are typically based on reactive automation rules that scale a cluster whenever some metric, e.g., the average CPU usage among instances, exceeds a predefined threshold. Tuning these rules becomes particularly cumbersome when scaling-up a cluster involves non-negligible times to bootstrap new instances, as it happens frequently in production cloud services.

title: Automated SpectroPhotometric Image REDuction ( ASPIRED ) astro-scrappy ( van Dokkum 2001 ; McCully et al. 2018 ) Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , ccdproc ( Craig et al. 2017 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) plotly ( Plot
creator: Marco C. Lam, Robert J. Smith, Iair Arcavi, Iain A. Steele, Josh Veitch-Michaelis, Lukasz Wyrzykowski
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Marco C. Lam, Robert J. Smith, Iair Arcavi, Iain A. Steele, Josh Veitch-Michaelis, Lukasz Wyrzykowski. We provide a suite of public open-source spectral data-reduction software to rapidly obtain scientific products from all forms of long-slit-like spectroscopic observations. Automated SpectroPhotometric REDuction ( ASPIRED ) is a Python -based spectral data-reduction toolkit. It is designed to be a general toolkit with high flexibility for users to refine and optimize their data-reduction routines for the individual characteristics of their instruments.

title: Symbolic spectral decomposition of 3x3 matrices
creator: Michal HABERA, Andreas ZILIAN
description: Abstract Spectral decomposition of matrices is a recurring and important task in applied mathematics, physics and engineering. Many application problems require the consideration of matrices of size three with spectral decomposition over the real numbers. If the functional dependence of the spectral decomposition on the matrix elements has to be preserved, then closed-form solution approaches must be considered.

title: Parity and Time-reversal Invariance Violation In Neutron-Nucleus Scattering
creator: V. V. Flambaum 1,2,3, A. J. Mansour 1
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by V. V. Flambaum 1,2,3, A. J. Mansour 1. Parity violating (PV) as well as parity and time-reversal invariance violating (PTRIV) effects are enhanced a million times in neutron reactions near p p -wave compound resonances. We present the calculation of such effects using a statistical theory based on the properties of chaotic eigenstates and discuss a possibility to extract the strength constants of PTRIV interactions from the experimental data, including nucleon-nucleon and pion-nucleon CP-violating interactions, the QCD θ \theta -term and the quark chromo-EDM.

title: Distributed Extended Object Tracking Information Filter Over Sensor Networks Journal: International Journal of Nonlinear and Robust Control
creator: Zhifei Li, Yan Liang, Linfeng Xu, Shuli Ma
description: Abstract This work aims to design a distributed extended object tracking (EOT) system over a realistic network, where both the extent and kinematics are required to retain consensus within the entire network. To this end, we resort to the multiplicative error model (MEM) that allows the extent parameters of perpendicular axis-symmetric objects to have individual uncertainty.

title: Beyond PRNU: Learning Robust Device-Specific Fingerprint for Source Camera Identification
creator: Manisha, Chang-Tsun Li, Xufeng Lin, Karunakar A. Kotegar
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Manisha, Chang-Tsun Li, Xufeng Lin, Karunakar A. Kotegar. Source camera identification tools assist image forensic investigators to associate an image in question with a suspect camera. Various techniques have been developed based on the analysis of the subtle traces left in the images during the acquisition. The Photo Response Non Uniformity (PRNU) noise pattern caused by sensor imperfections has been proven to be an effective way to identify the source camera.

title: Deployment Optimization for Shared e-Mobility Systems with Multi-agent Deep Neural Search
creator: Man Luo, Bowen Du, Konstantin Klemmer, Hongming Zhu, Hongkai Wen
description: Abstract Shared e-mobility services have been widely tested and piloted in cities across the globe, and already woven into the fabric of modern urban planning. This paper studies a practical yet important problem in those systems: how to deploy and manage their infrastructure across space and time, so that the services are ubiquitous to the users while sustainable in profitability.

title: Multiple–index Nonstationary Time Series Models: Robust Estimation Theory and Practice
creator: Chaohua Dong, Jiti Gao, Bin Peng, Yundong Tu, [5mm] Zhongnan University of Economics, Law, China
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chaohua Dong, Jiti Gao, Bin Peng, Yundong Tu, [5mm] Zhongnan University of Economics, Law, China. This paper proposes a class of parametric multiple-index time series models that involve linear combinations of time trends, stationary variables and unit root processes as regressors. The inclusion of the three different types of time series, along with the use of a multiple-index structure for these variables to circumvent the curse of dimensionality, is due to both theoretical and practical considerations.

title: Legendre pairs of lengths ℓ ≡ 0 ​ ( mod ​ 5 ) \ell\equiv 0\,\,(\mathrm{mod}\;5) Thanks: West Virginia University Morgantown, West Virginia 26506, USA
creator: Ilias Kotsireas Christoph Koutschan Dursun Bulutoglu
description: Abstract By assuming a type of balance for length ℓ = 87 \ell=87 and non-trivial subgroups of multiplier groups of Legendre pairs (LPs) for length ℓ = 85 \ell=85 , we find LPs of these lengths. We then study the power spectral density (PSD) values of m m compressions of LPs of length 5 ​ m 5m .

title: Computing Stackelberg Equilibrium with Memory in Sequential Games
creator: Aditya Aradhye, Branislav Bošanský, Michael Hlaváček
description: Abstract Stackelberg equilibrium is a solution concept that describes optimal strategies to commit: Player 1 ( the leader ) first commits to a strategy that is publicly announced, then Player 2 ( the follower ) plays a best response to the leader’s commitment.

title: Continual Adaptation of Semantic Segmentation using Complementary 2D-3D Data Representations
creator: Jonas Frey, Hermann Blum, Francesco Milano, Roland Siegwart, Cesar Cadena
description: Abstract Semantic segmentation networks are usually pre-trained once and not updated during deployment. As a consequence, misclassifications commonly occur if the distribution of the training data deviates from the one encountered during the robot’s operation. We propose to mitigate this problem by adapting the neural network to the robot’s environment during deployment, without any need for external supervision.

title: Realtime Trajectory Smoothing with Neural Nets
creator: Shohei Fujii, Quang-Cuong Pham
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shohei Fujii, Quang-Cuong Pham. In order to safely and efficiently collaborate with humans, industrial robots need the ability to alter their motions quickly to react to sudden changes in the environment, such as an obstacle appearing across a planned trajectory. In Realtime Motion Planning, obstacles are detected in real time through a vision system, and new trajectories are planned with respect to the current positions of the obstacles, and immediately executed on the robot.

title: Discriminator Synthesis: On reusing the other half of Generative Adversarial Networks
creator: Diego Porres
description: Abstract Generative Adversarial Networks have long since revolutionized the world of computer vision and, tied to it, the world of art. Arduous efforts have gone into fully utilizing and stabilizing training so that outputs of the Generator network have the highest possible fidelity, but little has gone into using the Discriminator after training is complete.

title: Fiducial cross sections for the lepton-pair-plus-photon decay mode in Higgs production up to NNLO QCD Preprint: ZU-TH 52/21, KA-TP-23-2021, IPPP/21/42, P3H-21-078, CERN-TH-2021-165
creator: X. Chen a,b , T. Gehrmann c , E.W.N. Glover d , A. Huss e
description: Abstract The rare three-body decay of a Higgs boson to a lepton-antilepton pair and a photon is starting to become experimentally accessible at the LHC. We investigate how higher-order QCD corrections to the dominant gluon-fusion production process impact on the fiducial cross sections in this specific Higgs decay mode for electrons and muons.

title: A geometrically exact model for thin magneto-elastic shells
creator: Matteo Pezzulla, Dong Yan, Pedro M. Reis
description: Abstract We develop a reduced model for hard-magnetic, thin, linear-elastic shells that can be actuated through an external magnetic field, with geometrically exact strain measures. Assuming a reduced kinematics based on the Kirchhoff-Love assumption, we derive a reduced two-dimensional magneto-elastic energy that can be minimized through numerical analysis.

title: Effective Guessing Has Unlikely Consequences
creator: András Z. Salamon, Michael Wehar
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by András Z. Salamon, Michael Wehar. A classic result of Paul, Pippenger, Szemerédi and Trotter states that 𝖣𝖳𝖨𝖬𝖤 ⁡ ( n ) ⊊ 𝖭𝖳𝖨𝖬𝖤 ⁡ ( n ) \mathsf{DTIME}(n)\subsetneq\mathsf{NTIME}(n) . The natural question then arises: could the inclusion 𝖣𝖳𝖨𝖬𝖤 ⁡ ( t ⁡ ( n ) ) ⊆ 𝖭𝖳𝖨𝖬𝖤 ⁡ ( n ) \mathsf{DTIME}(t(n))\subseteq\mathsf{NTIME}(n) hold for some superlinear time-constructible function t ⁡ ( n ) t(n) ?

title: Applications of intersection theory: from maximum likelihood to chromatic polynomials
creator: Rodica Andreea Dinu, Mateusz Michałek and Tim Seynnaeve
description: Abstract . Recently, we have witnessed tremendous applications of algebraic intersection theory to branches of mathematics, that previously seemed very distant. In this article we review some of them. Our aim is to provide a unified approach to the results e.g.

title: BERT-DRE: BERT with Deep Recursive Encoder for Natural Language Sentence Matching
creator: Ehsan Tavan, Ali Rahmati, Maryam Najafi, Saeed Bibak, Zahed Rahmati
description: Abstract This paper presents a deep neural architecture, for Natural Language Sentence Matching (NLSM) by adding a deep recursive encoder to BERT so called BERT with Deep Recursive Encoder (BERT-DRE). Our analysis of model behavior shows that BERT still does not capture the full complexity of text, so a deep recursive encoder is applied on top of BERT.

title: Experimental and computational approaches to study the high temperature thermoelectric properties of novel topological semimetal CoSi
creator: Shamim Sk 1,, Nisha Shahi 2, Sudhir K. Pandey 3,
description: Abstract Here, we study the thermoelectric properties of topological semimetal CoSi in the temperature range 300 − 800 300-800 K by using combined experimental and density functional theory (DFT) based methods. CoSi is synthesized using arc melting technique and the Rietveld refinement gives the lattice parameters of a = b = c = 4.445 Å .

title: Interpolation Estimator for Infinite Sets of Random Vectors
creator: A. Torokhti
description: Abstract We propose an approach to the filtering of infinite sets of stochastic signals, K Y K_{{}_{Y}} and K X K_{{}_{X}} . The known Wiener-type approach cannot be applied to infinite sets of signals. Even in the case when K Y K_{{}_{Y}} and K X K_{{}_{X}} are finite sets, the computational work associated with the Wiener approach becomes unreasonably hard.

title: Unsupervised detection and open-set classification of fast-ramped flexibility activation events
creator: Nils Müller, Carsten Heinrich, Kai Heussen, Henrik W. Bindner
description: Abstract The continuous electrification of the mobility and heating sectors adds much-needed flexibility to the power system. However, flexibility utilization also introduces new challenges to distribution system operators, who need mechanisms to supervise flexibility activations and monitor their effect on distribution network operation.

title: A radiation transfer model for the Milky Way. II The global properties and large scale structure 2016 A radiation transfer model for the Milky Way. II The global properties and large scale structure – 3
creator: Giovanni Natale, Cristina C. Popescu, Mark Rushton, Ruizhi Yang, Jordan J. Thirlwall, Dumitru Pricopi
description: Abstract We obtained an axi-symmetric model for the large-scale distribution of stars and dust in the Milky Way (MW) using a radiative transfer code that can account for the existing near-infrared (NIR)/mid-infrared/submm all-sky emission maps of our Galaxy. We find that the MW has a star-formation rate of SFR = 1.25 ± 0.2 ​ M ⊙ {\rm SFR}=1.25\pm 0.

title: Primordial Helical Magnetic Fields from Inflation?
description: Abstract We revisit the mechanism of helical magnetogenesis during inflation with a parity violating interaction using the formalism of stochastic inflation. One of the polarization of the gauge field undergoes tachyonic growth leading to the generation of helical magnetic fields. We obtain the Langevin equations associated with the electromagnetic fields which are in the form of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck stochastic differential equations.

title: Learning Implicit Sentiment in Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis with Supervised Contrastive Pre-Training
creator: Zhengyan Li, Yicheng Zou, Chong Zhang, Qi Zhang, Zhongyu Wei
description: Abstract Aspect-based sentiment analysis aims to identify the sentiment polarity of a specific aspect in product reviews. We notice that about 30% of reviews do not contain obvious opinion words, but still convey clear human-aware sentiment orientation, which is known as implicit sentiment. However, recent neural network-based approaches paid little attention to implicit sentiment entailed in the reviews.

title: Local Structure and effective Dimensionality of Time Series Data Sets
creator: Monika Dörfler, Franz Luef, Eirik Skrettingland
description: Abstract . The goal of this paper is to develop novel tools for understanding the local structure of systems of functions, e.g. time-series data points, such as the total correlation function, the Cohen class of the data set, the data operator and the average lack of concentration.

title: Knödel walks in a Böhm-Hornik environment
creator: Helmut Prodinger
description: Abstract . Ideas of Knödel and Böhm-Hornik about walks in certain graphs, resembling the classical symmetric random walk on the integers, are combined. All the relevant generating functions (although occasionally quite involved) are made fully explicit. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 05A15 1.

title: Thermo-magneto-electric transport through a torsion dislocation in a type I Weyl Semimetal
creator: Daniel Bonilla, Enrique Muñoz, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido
description: Abstract We study electronic and thermoelectric transport in a type I Weyl semimetal nanojunction, with a torsional dislocation defect, in the presence of an external magnetic field parallel to the dislocation axis. The defect is modeled in a cylindrical geometry, as a combination of a gauge field accounting for torsional strain, and a delta-potential barrier for the lattice mismatch effect.

title: Spherical accretion in alternative theories of gravity Note: Accepted for publication in ApJ
creator: Adam Bauer Alejandro Cárdenas-Avendaño Charles F. Gammie Nicolás Yunes
description: Abstract The groundbreaking image of the black hole at the center of the M87 galaxy has raised questions at the intersection of observational astronomy and black hole physics. How well can the radius of a black hole shadow can be measured, and can this measurement be used to distinguish general relativity from other theories of gravity?

title: Shell-model study of titanium isotopic chain with chiral two- and three-body forces
creator: L. Coraggio, G. De Gregorio, A. Gargano, N. Itaco, T. Fukui, Y. Z. Ma, F. R. Xu
description: Abstract The even-even Ti isotopic chain, from A = 42 A=42 to 70, has been studied within the nuclear shell-model framework by employing an effective Hamiltonian which is derived by way of many-body perturbation theory from a chiral potential with two- and three-body forces, and includes three-body contributions which account for Pauli principle violations in nuclei with more than two

title: Anomalous excitations of atomically crafted quantum magnets
creator: Sascha Brinker 1,∗ , Felix Küster 2 , Stuart S. P. Parkin 2 , Paolo Sessi 2 , Samir Lounis 1,3,∗
description: Abstract High energy resolution spectroscopic studies of quantum magnets proved extremely valuable in accessing magnetodynamics quantities, such as energy barriers, magnetic interactions and lifetime of excited states. Here, we explore the evolution of a new flavor of low-energy spin-excitations for quantum spins coupled to an electron bath.

title: The Psychological Gains from COVID-19 Vaccination: Who Benefits the Most? Thanks: Manuel Bagues, University of Warwick, CEPR, IZA and J-Pal; email: manuel.bagues@warwick.ac.uk; Velichka Dimitrova, University of Warwick; email: velichka.dimitrova.1@warwick.ac.uk. We thank Andrew Oswald, Thiemo Fetzer
creator: Manuel Bagues Velichka Dimitrova
description: Abstract We quantify the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on psychological well-being using information from a large-scale panel survey representative of the UK population. Exploiting exogenous variation in the timing of vaccinations, we find that vaccination increases psychological well-being (GHQ-12) by 0.12 standard deviation, compensating for around one half of the overall decrease caused by the pandemic.

title: Gravitational atmospheric tides as a probe of Titan’s interior: Application to Dragonfly
creator: B. Charnay, G. Tobie, S. Lebonnois, R. D. Lorenz
description: Abstract Context. Saturn’s massive gravity is expected to causes a tide in Titan’s atmosphere, producing a surface pressure variation through the orbit of Titan and tidal winds in the troposphere. The future Dragonfly mission could analyse this exotic meteorological phenomenon. Aims.

title: Deep Least Squares Alignment for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
creator: Youshan Zhang, Brian D. Davison
description: Abstract Unsupervised domain adaptation leverages rich information from a labeled source domain to model an unlabeled target domain. Existing methods attempt to align the cross-domain distributions. However, the statistical representations of the alignment of the two domains are not well addressed.
