description: Abstract Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to capture a wide variety of interactions between pairs of objects, which is essential for full scene understanding. Existing SGG methods trained on the entire set of relations fail to acquire complex reasoning about visual and textual correlations due to various biases in training data.

title: Collectivity of J / ψ J/\psi Mesons in Heavy-Ion Collisions
creator: Min He 1 , Biaogang Wu 2 , and Ralf Rapp 2
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Min He 1 , Biaogang Wu 2 , and Ralf Rapp 2. The production of J / ψ J/\psi mesons in heavy-ion collisions at the Large Hadron Collider is believed to be dominated by the recombination of charm and anti-charm quarks in a hot QCD medium.

title: A model of semantic completion in generative episodic memory
creator: Zahra Fayyaz, Aya Altamimi, Sen Cheng, Laurenz Wiskott 1 Institute for Neural Computation, Ruhr University Bochum, Germany * laurenz.wiskott@rub.de
description: Abstract Many different studies have suggested that episodic memory is a generative process, but most computational models adopt a storage view. In this work, we propose a computational model for generative episodic memory. It is based on the central hypothesis that the hippocampus stores and retrieves selected aspects of an episode as a memory trace, which is necessarily incomplete.

title: Exact and many-body perturbation solutions of the Hubbard model applied to linear chains.
creator: Antoine Honet, Luc Henrard, Vincent Meunier
description: Abstract This study reports on the accuracy of the GW approximation for the treatment of the Hubbard model, compared to exact diagonalization (ED) results. GW is part of the more general Green’s functions approach used to develop many-body approximations (GFMBA).

title: Fabric-SCF: A Blockchain-based Secure Storage and Access Control Scheme for Supply Chain Finance
creator: Dun Li ID, Dezhi Han ID, Noel Crespi, Roberto Minerva ID, Zhijie Sun ID
description: Abstract Supply chain finance(SCF) is committed to providing credit for small and medium-sized enterprises(SMEs) with low credit lines and small financing scales. The resulting financial credit data and related business transaction data are highly confidential and private. However, traditional SCF management schemes mostly use third-party platforms and centralized designs, which cannot achieve highly reliable secure storage and fine-grained access control.

title: Radial overlap correction to superallowed 0 + → 0 + 0^{+}\to 0^{+} nuclear β \beta decays using the shell model with Hartree-Fock radial wave functions
creator: L. Xayavong, N. A. Smirnova
description: Abstract The radial overlap correction, δ R ​ O \delta_{RO} is re-examined for 30 superallowed 0 + → 0 + 0^{+}\to 0^{+} nuclear β \beta decays using the shell model with Hartree-Fock (HF) radial wave functions. Our mean-field calculation is based on the effective Skyrme interaction including Coulomb, Charge-Symmetry-Breaking (CSB) and Charge-Independence-Breaking (CIB) terms.

title: GeoNeRF: Generalizing NeRF with Geometry Priors
creator: Mohammad Mahdi Johari, Yann Lepoittevin, François Fleuret
description: Abstract We present GeoNeRF, a generalizable photorealistic novel view synthesis method based on neural radiance fields. Our approach consists of two main stages: a geometry reasoner and a renderer. To render a novel view, the geometry reasoner first constructs cascaded cost volumes for each nearby source view.

title: A Sub-Picosecond Digitally-Controlled Phase Delay
creator: Y. Tousi \note Corresponding author
description: Abstract The use of precision timing measurements will be a major tool at the HL-LHC, where it will be used to suppress pile-up and to search for long-lived particles. To control a reference clock with sub-picosecond accuracy, we have fabricated in the TSMC 65 nm process a digitally controlled phase shifter.

title: X-ray characterisation of the massive galaxy cluster ClG-J104803.7+313843 at z=0.76 with XMM- Newton
creator: I. Bartalucci, F. Gastaldello, E. Piconcelli, L. Zappacosta, M. Rossetti, S. Ghizzardi, S. De Grandi, S. Molendi, Marco Laurenti
description: Abstract We present the characterisation of the massive cluster ClG-J104803.7+313843 at z=0.76 performed using a serendipitous XMM- Newton observation. High redshift and massive objects represent an ideal laboratory to benchmark our understanding of how cluster form and assembly formation driven mainly by gravity.

title: Actions and semi-direct products in categories of groups with action
creator: Tamar Datuashvili, Tunçar Þahan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tamar Datuashvili, Tunçar Þahan. Derived actions in the category of groups with action on itself 𝐆𝐫 ∙ \mathbf{Gr}^{\bullet} are defined and described. This category plays a crucial role in the solution of Loday’s two problems stated in the literature.

title: Dolbeault-type complexes on G 2 G_{2} - and Spin ⁡ ( 7 ) \mathrm{Spin}(7) -manifolds
creator: Xue Zhang
description: Abstract There are three types of Dolbeault complexes arising from representations of holonomy group on a Riemannian manifold, two of which are dual to each other. Such a complex is elliptic if and only if its generator satisfies an algebraic condition. We list all Dolbeault complexes on compact G 2 G_{2} - and Spin ⁡ ( 7 ) \mathrm{Spin}(7) -manifolds.

title: Non-local thermodynamic equilibrium spectral analysis of five hot, hydrogen-deficient pre-white dwarfs
creator: Klaus Werner, Nicole Reindl, Matti Dorsch, Stephan Geier, Ulisse Munari, Roberto Raddi
description: Abstract Hot, compact, hydrogen-deficient pre-white dwarfs (pre-WDs) with effective temperatures of T eff T_{\mathrm{eff}} > > 70 000 K and a surface gravity of 5.0 < < log ⁡ g \log g < < 7.0 are rather rare objects despite recent and ongoing surveys.

title: Using Fictitious Class Representations to Boost Discriminative Zero-Shot Learners
creator: Mohammed Dabbah, Ran El-Yaniv
description: Abstract Focusing on discriminative zero-shot learning, in this work we introduce a novel mechanism that dynamically augments during training the set of seen classes to produce additional fictitious classes. These fictitious classes diminish the model’s tendency to fixate during training on attribute correlations that appear in the training set but will not appear in newly exposed classes.

title: Hypergraph Representation via Axis-Aligned Point-Subspace Cover
creator: Oksana Firman, Joachim Spoerhase
description: Abstract A k k -hypergraph is a k k -partite k k -uniform hypergraph, that is, a hypergraph with a partition of vertices into k k parts such that each hyperedge contains exactly one vertex of each part. We propose a new geometric representation of k k -hypergraphs.

title: Complexity and Approximability of Edge-Vertex Domination in UDG
creator: Vishwanath Reddy Singireddy, Manjanna Basappa
description: Abstract Given an undirected graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , a vertex v ∈ V v\in V is edge-vertex (ev) dominated by an edge e ∈ E e\in E if v v is either incident to e e or incident to an adjacent edge of e e .

title: Teaching Undergraduate Students to Think Like Real-World Systems Engineers: A Technology-Based Hybrid Learning Approach
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . A hybrid teaching approach that relies on combining the principles of Project Based Learning and Team Based Learning has been designed in an electronic engineering module during the past five years. Our motivation was to expose students to real-world authentic engineering problems and to direct students away from the classical “banking” teaching approach, with a view to developing their systems engineering skills via deeper and more collaborative learning.

title: Localization persisting under aperiodic driving
creator: Hongzheng Zhao, Florian Mintert, Johannes Knolle, Roderich Moessner
description: Abstract Introduction.– Closed quantum many-body systems with time-dependent (‘driven’) Hamiltonians tend to absorb energy until they reach a featureless ‘infinite temperature’ state 2014PhRvE..90a2110L ; abanin2015exponentially ; kuwahara2016 . This heat death can be prevented if a sufficient number of integrals of motion is present.

title: Optimal Estimation of Schatten Norms of a rectangular Matrix
creator: Solène Thépaut and Nicolas Verzelen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Solène Thépaut and Nicolas Verzelen. We consider the twin problems of estimating the effective rank and the Schatten norms ‖ 𝐀 ‖ s \|\mathbf{A}\|_{s} of a rectangular p × q p\times q matrix 𝐀 \mathbf{A} from noisy observations. When s s is an even integer, we introduce a polynomial-time estimator of ‖ 𝐀 ‖ s \|\mathbf{A}\|_{s} that achieves the minimax rate ( p ​ q ) 1 / 4 (pq)^{1/4} .

title: Training a quantum measurement device to discriminate unknown non-orthogonal quantum states
creator: D. Concha, L. Pereira, L. Zambrano, A. Delgado
description: Abstract Here, we study the problem of decoding information transmitted through unknown quantum states. We assume that Alice encodes an alphabet into a set of orthogonal quantum states, which are then transmitted to Bob. However, the quantum channel that mediates the transmission maps the orthogonal states into non-orthogonal states, possibly mixed.

title: A novel measurement of marginal Alfvén Eigenmode stability during high power auxiliary heating in JET
creator: R.A. Tinguely 1, N. Fil 2, P.G. Puglia 3, S. Dowson 2, M. Porkolab 1, V. Guillemot 4, M. Podestà 5, M. Baruzzo 2, R. Dumont 6, A. Fasoli 3, M. Fitzgerald 2, Ye.O. Kazakov 7, M.F.F. Nave 8, M. Nocente 9 10, J. Ongena 7, S.E. Sharapov 2, Ž. Štancar 11, JET Contributors*
description: Abstract The interaction of Alfvén Eigenmodes (AEs) and energetic particles is one of many important factors determining the success of future tokamaks. In JET, eight in-vessel antennas were installed to actively probe stable AEs with frequencies ranging 25 − 250 ​ kHz 25{-}250~\mathrm{kHz} and toroidal mode numbers | n | < 20 |n|<20 .

title: Quantization of a Black-Hole Gravity: Geometrodynamics and the Quantum Phase-Space Formalism
creator: Carla R. Almeida, Denis C. Rodrigues
description: Abstract Quantum gravity is effective in domains where both quantum effects and gravity are essential, such as in the vicinity of space-time singularities. This paper will investigate the quantization of a black-hole gravity, particularly the region surrounding the singularity at the origin of the coordinate system.

title: Impurity with a resonance in the vicinity of the Fermi energy
creator: Mikhail Maslov, Mikhail Lemeshko, Artem G. Volosniev
description: Abstract We study an impurity with a resonance level whose position coincides with the Fermi energy of the surrounding Fermi gas. An impurity causes a rapid variation of the scattering phase shift for fermions at the Fermi surface, introducing a new characteristic length scale into the problem.

title: Job Recommender Systems: A Review
description: Abstract This paper provides a review of the job recommender system (JRS) literature published in the past decade (2011-2021). Compared to previous literature reviews, we put more emphasis on contributions that incorporate the temporal and reciprocal nature of job recommendations.

title: h h -almost Ricci-Yamabe solitons in paracontact geometry
creator: Arpan Sardar*, Uday Chand De and Cihan Özgür
description: Abstract . In this article, we classify h h -almost Ricci-Yamabe solitons in paracontact geometry. In particular, we characterize para-Kenmotsu manifolds satisfying h h -almost Ricci-Yamabe solitons and 3-dimensional para-Kenmotsu manifolds obeying h h -almost gradient Ricci-Yamabe solitons. Next, we classify para-Sasakian manifolds admitting h h -almost Ricci-Yamabe solitons and h h -almost gradient Ricci-Yamabe solitons.

title: Graph Auto-Encoders for Financial Clustering
creator: Edward Turner
description: Abstract Deep learning has shown remarkable results on Euclidean data (e.g. audio, images, text) however this type of data is limited in the amount of relational information it can hold. In mathematics we can model more general relational data in a graph structure while retaining Euclidean data as associated node or edge features.

title: VL-LTR: Learning Class-wise Visual-Linguistic Representation for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition
creator: Changyao Tian 1∗†, Wenhai Wang 3∗, Xizhou Zhu 2∗, Jifeng Dai 2 🖂, Yu Qiao 3, 1 Chinese University of Hong Kong 2 SenseTime 3 Shanghai AI Laboratory tcyhost@buaa.edu.cn {wangwenhai, qiaoyu}@pjlab.org.cn, {zhuwalter, daijifeng}@sensetime.com
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Changyao Tian 1∗†, Wenhai Wang 3∗, Xizhou Zhu 2∗, Jifeng Dai 2 🖂, Yu Qiao 3, 1 Chinese University of Hong Kong 2 SenseTime 3 Shanghai AI Laboratory tcyhost@buaa.edu.cn {wangwenhai, qiaoyu}@pjlab.org.cn, {zhuwalter, daijifeng}@sensetime.com. Recently, computer vision foundation models such as CLIP and ALI-GN, have shown impressive generalization capabilities on various downstream tasks. But their abilities to deal with the long-tailed data still remain to be proved.

title: The diverse cold molecular gas contents, morphologies, and kinematics of type-2 quasars as seen by ALMA
creator: C. Ramos Almeida, M. Bischetti, S. García-Burillo, A. Alonso-Herrero, A. Audibert, C. Cicone, C. Feruglio, C. N. Tadhunter, J. C. S. Pierce, M. Pereira-Santaella, P. S. Bessiere
description: Abstract We present CO(2 − - 1) and adjacent continuum observations of seven nearby radio-quiet type-2 quasars (QSO2s) obtained with ALMA at ∼ \sim 0.2″ resolution (370 pc at z ∼ \sim 0.1). These QSO2s are luminous (L [ OIII ] > {}_{\rm[OIII]}> 10 L ☉ 8.5 ∼ {}^{8.

title: Glass-box model representation of seismic failure mode prediction for conventional RC shear walls
creator: Zeynep Tuna Deger, Ph.D, Gulsen Taskin Kaya, Ph.D
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zeynep Tuna Deger, Ph.D, Gulsen Taskin Kaya, Ph.D. The recent surge in earthquake engineering is the use of machine learning methods to develop predictive models for structural behavior. Complex black-box models are typically used for decision making to achieve high accuracy; however, as important as high accuracy, it is essential for engineers to understand how the model makes the decision and verify that the model is physically meaningful.

title: Machine learning-based porosity estimation from spectral decomposed seismic data
creator: Honggeun Jo, Yongchae Cho, Michael Pyrcz, Hewei Tang, Pengcheng Fu
description: Abstract 1 Abstract Estimating porosity models via seismic data is challenging due to the signal noise and insufficient resolution of seismic data. Although impedance inversion is often used by combining with well logs, several hurdles remain to retrieve sub-seismic scale porosity. As an alternative, we propose a machine learning-based workflow to convert seismic data to porosity models.

title: Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators: Efficient Token Mixers for Transformers
creator: John Guibas, Morteza Mardani, Zongyi Li, Andrew Tao, Anima Aanandkumar, Bryan Catanzaro, NVIDIA, California Institute of Technology, Stanford University jtguibas@stanford.edu , {mmardani,zongyil,atao,bcatanzaro,aanandkumar}@nvidia.com
description: Abstract Vision transformers have delivered tremendous success in representation learning. This is primarily due to effective token mixing through self-attention. However, this scales quadratically with the number of pixels, which becomes infeasible for high-resolution inputs. To cope with this challenge, we propose Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNO) as an efficient token mixer that learns to mix in the Fourier domain.

title: Salt-fingering in seasonally ice-covered lakes
description: Abstract When ice forms on lakes, dissolved salts are rejected, which can lead to under-ice salt-finger formation. We performed a series of laboratory experiments to visualize these fingers. While we detected salt-fingers in our camera recordings, the signal of these fingers is nearly absent in the temperature record.

title: From molecular to multi-asperity contacts: how roughness bridges the friction scale gap
creator: Lucas Frérot, Alexia Crespo, Jaafar A. El-Awady, Mark O. Robbins, Juliette Cayer-Barrioz, Denis Mazuyer
description: Abstract Friction is a pervasive phenomenon that affects the mechanical response of natural and man-made systems alike, from vascular catheterization to geological faults responsible for earthquakes. While friction stems from the fundamental interactions between atoms at a contact interface, its best descriptions at the macroscopic scale remain phenomenological.

title: Multi-criticality and related bifurcation in accretion discs around non-rotating black holes – an analytical study
creator: Arpan Krishna Mitra, Aishee Chakraborty, Pratik Tarafdar, Tapas Kumar Das
description: Abstract Low angular momentum, general relativistic, axially symmetric accretion of hydrodynamic fluid onto Schwarzschild black holes may undergo more than one critical transition. To obtain the stationary integral solutions corresponding to such multi-critical accretion flow, one needs to employ numerical solutions of the corresponding fluid dynamics equations.

title: Finding Geodesics on Surfaces Using Taylor Expansion of Exponential Map
creator: E. Peyghan, E. Sharahi, A. Baghban
description: Abstract Our aim in this paper, is to construct a numerical algorithm using Taylor expansion of exponential map to find geodesic joining two points on a 2-dimensional surface for which a Riemannian metric is defined. Keywords: Euclidean space, exponential map, geodesic, navigation problem, Riemannian manifold, Taylor expansion.

title: A NOVEL GPR-BASED PREDICTION MODEL FOR CYCLIC BACKBONE CURVES OF REINFORCED CONCRETE SHEAR WALLS
creator: Zeynep Tuna Deger, Ph.D, Gulsen Taskin Kaya, Ph.D
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zeynep Tuna Deger, Ph.D, Gulsen Taskin Kaya, Ph.D. Backbone curves are used to characterize nonlinear responses of structural elements by simplifying the cyclic force – deformation relationships. Accurate modeling of cyclic behavior can be achieved with a reliable backbone curve model. In this paper, a novel machine learning-based model is proposed to predict the backbone curve of reinforced concrete shear (structural) walls based on key wall design properties.

title: Conormal homology of manifolds with corners Thanks: This work was carried out during a research stay of the second author at Univerity of Göttingen funded by the German Science Foundation RTG “Fourier analysis and spectral theory”
creator: Thomas Schick, Mario Velásquez
description: Abstract . Given a manifold with corners X X , we associates to it the corner structure simplicial complex Σ X \Sigma_{X} . Its reduced K-homology is isomorphic to the K-theory of the C ∗ C^{*} -algebra 𝒦 b ​ ( X ) \mathcal{K}_{b}(X) of b-compact operators on X X .

title: Joint Wireless and Computing Resources Allocation in Multi-Cell MEC
creator: Ming Zeng
description: Abstract This paper addresses join wireless and computing resource allocation in mobile edge computing (MEC) systems with several access points and with the possibility that users connect to many access points, and utilize the computation capability of many servers at the same time. The problem of sum transmission energy minimization under response time constraints is considered.

title: Microscopical Justification of the Winterbottom problem for well-separated Lattices
creator: Paolo Piovano, Igor Velčić
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Paolo Piovano, Igor Velčić. We consider the discrete atomistic setting introduced in [ 25 ] to microscopically justify the continuum model related to the Winterbottom problem , i.e., the problem of determining the equilibrium shape of crystalline film drops resting on a substrate, and relax the rigidity assumption considered in [ 25 ] to characterize the wetting and dewetting regimes and to perform the discrete to continuum passage .

title: Spectrally Multiplexed Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
creator: Oriol Pietx-Casas, Gustavo Castro do Amaral, Tanmoy Chakraborty, Remon Berrevoets, Thomas Middelburg, Joshua Slater, Wolfgang Tittel
description: Abstract We explore the suitability of a Virtually-Imaged Phased Array (VIPA) as a Spectral-to-Spatial Mode-Mapper (SSMM) for applications in quantum communication such as a quantum repeater. To this end we demonstrate spectrally-resolved two-photon “Hong-Ou-Mandel” (HOM) interference. Spectral sidebands are generated on a common optical carrier and weak coherent pulses are prepared in each spectral mode.

title: The effect of substrate waviness on random sequential adsorption packing properties
creator: Piotr Kubala, Michał Cieśla
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Piotr Kubala, Michał Cieśla. Random sequential adsorption of spheres on a wavy surface was studied. It was determined how surface structure influences random packing properties such as the packing fraction, the kinetics of packing growth and the two-particle density correlation function. Until the substrate varies within the range one order of magnitude smaller than the particle’s diameter, the properties of the packings obtained do not differ significantly from those on a flat surface.

title: Entropic Gravity and Cosmology in Kaniadakis Statistics
description: Abstract By using the Kaniadakis statistics, we discuss the modifications of Newtonian gravity and radial velocity profile in the light of Verlinde’s formalism for gravitational entropy. After considering the implications of κ \kappa -statistics on the gravitational potential, it is shown that an accelerated universe may be obtained by considering the Friedmann first equation in this non- extensive statistics. N.

title: Predicting Document Coverage for Relation Extraction
creator: Sneha Singhania, Simon Razniewski, Gerhard Weikum
description: Abstract This paper presents a new task of predicting the coverage of a text document for relation extraction (RE): does the document contain many relational tuples for a given entity? Coverage predictions are useful in selecting the best documents for knowledge base construction with large input corpora.

title: On phase-space integrals with Heaviside functions Preprint: TTP-21-053 P3H-21-097 TUM-HEP-1376/21
creator: Daniel Baranowski, Maximilian Delto, Kirill Melnikov, Chen-Yu Wang
description: Abstract We discuss peculiarities that arise in the computation of real-emission contributions to observables that contain Heaviside functions. A prominent example of such a case is the zero-jettiness soft function in SCET, whose calculation at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order in perturbative QCD is an interesting problem.

title: Short Review: Pathology of the image big data era using electron microscopy
creator: Satoshi Kume
description: Abstract 1 Introduction -Fusion of Innovative Imaging Technology and Pathology- The human body is mysterious, consisting of innumerable fine and complex structures and a vast amount of information. The field of modern pathology has been systematized around the findings and observations obtained from light microscopy.

title: HIDDEN MARKOV MODELING OVER GRAPHS
creator: Mert Kayaalp, Virginia Bordignon, Stefan Vlaski, Ali H. Sayed
description: Abstract This work proposes a multi-agent filtering algorithm over graphs for finite-state hidden Markov models (HMMs), which can be used for sequential state estimation or for tracking opinion formation over dynamic social networks. We show that the difference from the optimal centralized Bayesian solution is asymptotically bounded for geometrically ergodic transition models.

title: Fixed Points Theorems in Hausdorff M-distance Spaces
creator: Vladyslav Babenko, Vira Babenko, Oleg Kovalenko
description: Abstract . We prove fixed point theorems in a space with a distance function that takes values in a partially ordered monoid. On the one hand, such an approach allows one to generalize some fixed point theorems in a broad class of spaces, including metric and uniform spaces.

title: Quantum transport of high-dimensional spatial information with a nonlinear detector
creator: Bereneice Sephton, Adam Vallés, Isaac Nape, Mitchell A. Cox, Fabian Steinlechner, Thomas Konrad, Juan P. Torres, Filippus S. Roux, Andrew Forbes
description: Abstract Information exchange between two distant parties, where information is shared without physically transporting it, is a crucial resource in future quantum networks. Doing so with high-dimensional states offers the promise of higher information capacity and improved resilience to noise, but progress to date has been limited.

title: Efficient Multi-Organ Segmentation Using SpatialConfiguartion-Net with Low GPU Memory Requirements
creator: Franz Thaler Gottfried Schatz Research Center: Biophysics Medical University of Graz, Austria and Institute of Computer Graphics and Vision Graz University of Technology, Austria franz.thaler@medunigraz.at, Christian Payer Institute of Computer Graphics and Vision Graz University of Technology, Aust
description: Abstract Even though many semantic segmentation methods exist that are able to perform well on many medical datasets, often, they are not designed for direct use in clinical practice. The two main concerns are generalization to unseen data with a different visual appearance, e.g.

title: Minimal pairs, inertia degrees, ramification degrees and implicit constant fields Thanks: This work was supported by the Post-Doctoral Fellowship of the National Board of Higher Mathematics, India.
creator: Arpan Dutta
description: Abstract . An extension ( K ⁡ ( X ) | K , v ) (K(X)|K,v) of valued fields is said to be valuation transcendental if we have equality in the Abhyankar inequality. Minimal pairs of definition are fundamental objects in the investigation of valuation transcendental extensions.

title: Contrastive Object-level Pre-training with Spatial Noise Curriculum Learning
creator: Chenhongyi Yang, Lichao Huang, Elliot J. Crowley
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chenhongyi Yang, Lichao Huang, Elliot J. Crowley. The goal of contrastive learning based pre-training is to leverage large quantities of unlabeled data to produce a model that can be readily adapted downstream. Current approaches revolve around solving an image discrimination task: given an anchor image, an augmented counterpart of that image, and some other images, the model must produce representations such that the distance between the anchor and its counterpart is small, and the distances between the anchor and the other images are large.

title: Emergent Pauli blocking in a weakly interacting Bose gas
creator: Federica Cataldini, Frederik Møller, Mohammadamin Tajik, João Sabino, Si-Cong Ji, Igor Mazets, Thomas Schweigler, Bernhard Rauer, Jörg Schmiedmayer
description: Abstract The relationship between many-body interactions and dimensionality is integral to numerous emergent quantum phenomena. A striking example is the Bose gas, which upon confinement to one dimension (1D) obeys an infinite set of conservation laws, prohibiting thermalization and constraining dynamics.

title: Towards Low-Cost and Efficient Malaria Detection
creator: Waqas Sultani, Wajahat Nawaz, Syed Javed, Muhammad Sohail Danish, Asma Saadia, Mohsen Ali
description: Abstract Malaria, a fatal but curable disease claims hundreds of thousands of lives every year. Early and correct diagnosis is vital to avoid health complexities, however, it depends upon the availability of costly microscopes and trained experts to analyze blood-smear slides.

title: Definition, detection, and tracking of persistent structures in atmospheric flows
creator: Johannes von Lindheim, Abhishek Harikrishnan, Tom Dörffel, Rupert Klein, Péter Koltai, Natalia Mikula, Annette Müller, Peter Névir, George Pacey, Robert Polzin, Nikki Vercauteren
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Johannes von Lindheim, Abhishek Harikrishnan, Tom Dörffel, Rupert Klein, Péter Koltai, Natalia Mikula, Annette Müller, Peter Névir, George Pacey, Robert Polzin, Nikki Vercauteren. Long-lived flow patterns in the atmosphere such as weather fronts, mid-latitude blockings or tropical cyclones often induce extreme weather conditions. As a consequence, their description, detection, and tracking has received increasing attention in recent years.

title: Latent Space Smoothing for Individually Fair Representations
creator: Momchil Peychev 1, Anian Ruoss 2, Mislav Balunović 1, Maximilian Baader 1, Martin Vechev 1
description: Abstract Fair representation learning transforms user data into a representation that ensures fairness and utility regardless of the downstream application. However, learning individually fair representations, i.e., guaranteeing that similar individuals are treated similarly, remains challenging in high-dimensional settings such as computer vision. In this work, we introduce LASSI, the first representation learning method for certifying individual fairness of high-dimensional data.

title: 3D shape sensing and deep learning-based segmentation of strawberries
creator: Justin Le Louëdec, Grzegorz Cielniak
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Justin Le Louëdec, Grzegorz Cielniak. Automation and robotisation of the agricultural sector are seen as a viable solution to socio-economic challenges faced by this industry. This technology often relies on intelligent perception systems providing information about crops, plants and the entire environment. The challenges faced by traditional 2D vision systems can be addressed by modern 3D vision systems which enable straightforward localisation of objects, size and shape estimation, or handling of occlusions.

title: Modular Information Flow through Ownership Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3519939.3523445 pldi22main-p150-p ISBN: 978-1-4503-9265-5/22/06 Conference: Proceedings of the 43rd ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Programming Language Design and Implementation; June 13–17, 2022; San Diego, CA, USA Procee
creator: Will Crichton, Marco Patrignani, Maneesh Agrawala, Pat Hanrahan
description: Abstract . Statically analyzing information flow, or how data influences other data within a program, is a challenging task in imperative languages. Analyzing pointers and mutations requires access to a program’s complete source. However, programs often use pre-compiled dependencies where only type signatures are available.

title: Model systematics in time domain tests of binary black hole evolution
creator: Shilpa Kastha, Collin D. Capano, Julian Westerweck, Miriam Cabero, Badri Krishnan, Alex B. Nielsen
description: Abstract We perform several consistency tests between different phases of binary black hole dynamics; the inspiral, the merger and the ringdown on the gravitational wave events GW150914 and GW170814. These tests are performed explicitly in the time domain, without any spectral leakage between the different phases.

title: Additive bases, coset covers, and non-vanishing linear maps
creator: János Nagy, Péter Pál Pach, István Tomon
description: Abstract Recently, the first two authors proved the Alon-Jaeger-Tarsi conjecture on non-vanishing linear maps, for large primes. We extend their ideas to address several other related conjectures. We prove the weak Additive Basis conjecture proposed by Szegedy, making a significant step towards the Additive Basis conjecture of Jaeger, Linial, Payan, and Tarsi.

title: Collective Behaviour of Composite Active Particles
creator: Joshua Eglinton, Mike I. Smith, Michael R. Swift
description: Abstract We describe simulations of active Brownian particles carried out to explore how dynamics and clustering are influenced by particle shape. Our particles are composed of four disks, held together by springs, whose relative size can be varied. These composite objects can be tuned smoothly from having a predominantly concave to a convex surface.

title: TMM-Fast: A Transfer Matrix Computation Package for Multilayer Thin-Film Optimization
creator: Alexander Luce, Ali Mahdavi, Florian Marquardt, Heribert Wankerl
description: Abstract Achieving the desired optical response from a multilayer thin-film structure over a broad range of wavelengths and angles of incidence can be challenging. An advanced thin-film structure can consist of multiple materials with different thicknesses and numerous layers. Design and optimization of complex thin-film structures with multiple variables is a computationally heavy problem that is still under active research.

description: Abstract A search has been performed for heavy resonances decaying to \PZ ​ \PZ \PZ\PZ or \PZ ​ \PW \PZ\PW and for axion-like particles (ALPs) mediating nonresonant \PZ ​ \PZ \PZ\PZ or \PZ ​ \PH \PZ\PH production, in final states with two charged leptons ( \Pell = \Pe , \Pgm \Pell=\Pe,\Pgm ) produced by the decay of a \PZ boson,

title: Neural Fields as Learnable Kernels for 3D Reconstruction
creator: Francis Williams, Zan Gojcic, Sameh Khamis, Denis Zorin, Joan Bruna, Sanja Fidler, Or Litany
description: Abstract We present Neural Kernel Fields: a novel method for reconstructing implicit 3D shapes based on a learned kernel ridge regression. Our technique achieves state-of-the-art results when reconstructing 3D objects and large scenes from sparse oriented points, and can reconstruct shape categories outside the training set with almost no drop in accuracy.

title: Magnetic correlations in infinite-layer nickelates: an experimental and theoretical multi-method study
creator: R. A. Ortiz 1,∗ , P. Puphal 1,∗ , M. Klett 1 , F. Hotz 2 , R. K. Kremer 1 , H. Trepka 1 , M. Hemmida 2 , H.-A. Krug von Nidda 2 , M. Isobe 1 , R. Khasanov 3 , H. Luetkens 3 , P. Hansmann 4 , B. Keimer 1 , T. Schäfer 1,† , and M. Hepting †,
description: Abstract We report a comprehensive study of magnetic correlations in LaNiO 2 , a parent compound of the recently discovered family of infinite-layer (IL) nickelate superconductors, using multiple experimental and theoretical methods. Our specific heat, muon-spin rotation (µSR), and magnetic susceptibility measurements on polycrystalline LaNiO 2 show that long-range magnetic order remains absent down to 2 K.

title: GMFlow: Learning Optical Flow via Global Matching
creator: Haofei Xu Jing Zhang Jianfei Cai Hamid Rezatofighi Dacheng Tao
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Haofei Xu Jing Zhang Jianfei Cai Hamid Rezatofighi Dacheng Tao. Learning-based optical flow estimation has been dominated with the pipeline of cost volume with convolutions for flow regression, which is inherently limited to local correlations and thus is hard to address the long-standing challenge of large displacements. To alleviate this, the state-of-the-art framework RAFT gradually improves its prediction quality by using a large number of iterative refinements, achieving remarkable performance but introducing linearly increasing inference time.

title: Approximate 3 3 -designs and partial decomposition of the Clifford group representation using transvections
creator: Tanmay Singal, Min-Hsiu Hsieh
description: Abstract We study a scheme to implement an asymptotic unitary 3 3 -design. The scheme implements a random Pauli once followed by the implementation of a random transvection Clifford by using state twirling. Thus the scheme is implemented in the form of a quantum channel.

title: Stochastic modulational instability in the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with colored random dispersion
creator: Andrea Armaroli, Guillaume Dujardin, Alexandre Kudlinski, Arnaud Mussot, Stefano Trillo, Stephan De Bièvre, Matteo Conforti
description: Abstract We study modulational instability (MI) in optical fibers with random group-velocity dispersion (GVD). We consider Gaussian and dichotomous colored stochastic processes. We resort to different analytical methods (namely, the cumulant expansion and the functional approach) and assess their reliability in estimating the MI gain of stochastic origin.

title: The Information Content of Projected Galaxy Fields 2021 The Information Content of Projected Galaxy Fields – 12
creator: Lucas Porth, Gary M. Bernstein, Robert E. Smith, Abigail J. Lee
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lucas Porth, Gary M. Bernstein, Robert E. Smith, Abigail J. Lee. The power spectrum of the nonlinearly evolved large-scale mass distribution recovers only a minority of the information available on the mass fluctuation amplitude. We investigate the recovery of this information in 2D “slabs” of the mass distribution averaged over ≈ 100 \approx 100 h − 1 h^{-1} Mpc along the line of sight, as might be obtained from photometric redshift surveys.

title: Applying the metallicity-dependent binary fraction to double white dwarf formation: Implications for LISA astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Price-Whelan et al. 2018 ) ; COSMIC ( Breivik et al. 2020b ) ; LEGWORK ( Wagg et al. 2021 ) ; matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) ; numpy ( van der Walt et a
creator: Sarah Thiele, Katelyn Breivik, Robyn E. Sanderson, Rodrigo Luger
description: Abstract Short-period double white dwarf (DWD) binaries will be the most prolific source of gravitational waves (GWs) for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). DWDs with GW frequencies below ∼ 1 ​ mHz \sim 1\,\rm{mHz} will be the dominant contributor to a stochastic foreground caused by overlapping GW signals.

title: Atomic and molecular gas from the epoch of reionization down to redshift 2 Preprint: U. Maio, e-mail: umberto.maio@inaf.it
creator: Umberto Maio, Céline Péroux, Benedetta Ciardi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Umberto Maio, Céline Péroux, Benedetta Ciardi. Cosmic gas makes up about 90% of baryonic matter in the Universe and H 2 is the closest molecule to star formation. In this work we study cold neutral gas and its H 2 component at different epochs, exploiting state-of-the-art hydrodynamic simulations that include time-dependent atomic and molecular non-equilibrium chemistry coupled to star formation, feedback effects, different UV backgrounds presented in the recent literature and a number of additional processes occurring during structure formation ( ColdSIM ).

title: Regularized bayesian best response learning in finite games
creator: Sayan Mukherjee and Souvik Roy
description: Abstract We introduce the notion of regularized Bayesian best response (RBBR) learning dynamic in heterogeneous population games. We obtain such a dynamic via perturbation by an arbitrary lower semicontinuous, strongly convex regularizer in Bayesian population games with finitely many strategies.

title: On the convex characterisation of the set of unital quantum channels
creator: Constantino Rodriguez-Ramos, Colin M. Wilmott
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the convex structure of the set of unital quantum channels. To do this, we introduce a novel framework to construct and characterise different families of low-rank unital quantum maps. In this framework, unital quantum maps are represented as a set of complex parameters on which we impose a set of constraints.

title: Gravitational wave sources in our Galactic backyard: Predictions for BHBH, BHNS and NSNS binaries detectable with LISA We used LEGWORK to evolve sources over time and calculate signal-to-noise ratios ( Wagg et al. 2021 ) . It is freely available at https://legwork.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ . Simulat
creator: T. Wagg, F.S. Broekgaarden, S.E. de Mink, N. Frankel, L.A.C. van Son, S. Justham
description: Abstract Future searches for gravitational waves from space will be sensitive to double compact objects (DCOs) in our Milky-Way. We present new simulations of the populations of double black holes (BHBHs), black hole neutron stars (BHNSs) and double neutron stars (NSNSs) that will be detectable by the planned space-based gravitational wave detector LISA.

title: Freeze-in, glaciation, and UV sensitivity from light mediators
creator: Nicolas Fernandez, Yonatan Kahn, and Jessie Shelton
description: Abstract Dark matter (DM) freeze-in through a light mediator is an appealing model with excellent detection prospects at current and future experiments. Light mediator freeze-in is UV-insensitive insofar as most DM is produced at late times, and thus the DM abundance does not depend on the unknown early evolution of our universe.

title: Interacting bosons in a triple well: Preface of many-body quantum chaos
creator: Karin Wittmann W, E. R. Castro, Angela Foerster, Lea F. Santos
description: Abstract Systems of interacting bosons in triple-well potentials are of significant theoretical and experimental interest. They are explored in contexts that range from quantum phase transitions and quantum dynamics to semiclassical analysis. Here, we systematically investigate the onset of quantum chaos in a triple-well model that moves away from integrability as its potential gets tilted.

title: Enhanced superconductivity and various edge modes in modulated t t - J J chains
creator: Yong-Feng Yang, Jing Chen, Chen Cheng, Hong-Gang Luo
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yong-Feng Yang, Jing Chen, Chen Cheng, Hong-Gang Luo. We numerically investigate the ground state of the extended t t - J J Hamiltonian with periodic local modulations in one dimension by using the density-matrix renormalization group method. Examining charge and spin excitation gaps, as well as the pair binding energy, with extrapolated results to the thermodynamic limit, we obtain a rich ground-state phase diagram consisting of the metallic state, the superconducting state, the phase separation, and insulating states at commensurate fillings.

title: Constraining the Evolution of Cataclysmic Variables via the Masses and Accretion Rates of their Underlying White Dwarfs 2021 Constraining the Evolution of Cataclysmic Variables via the Masses and Accretion Rates of their Underlying White Dwarfs – 51
creator: A. F. Pala, B. T. Gänsicke, D. Belloni, S. G. Parsons, T. R. Marsh, M. R. Schreiber, E. Breedt, C. Knigge, E. M. Sion, P. Szkody, D. Townsley, L. Bildsten, D. Boyd, M. J. Cook, D. De Martino, P. Godon, S. Kafka, V. Kouprianov, K. S. Long, B. Monard, G. Myers, P. Nelson, D. Nogami, A. Oksanen, R. Pic
description: Abstract We report on the masses ( M WD M_{\mathrm{WD}} ), effective temperatures ( T eff T_{\mathrm{eff}} ) and secular mean accretion rates ( ⟨ M ˙ ⟩ \langle\dot{M}\rangle ) of 43 cataclysmic variable (CV) white dwarfs, 42 of which were obtained from the combined analysis of their Hubble Space Telescope ultraviolet data with the parallaxes provided by the Early

title: Probing many-body localization by excited-state VQE
creator: Shuo Liu, Shi-Xin Zhang, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Shengyu Zhang, Hong Yao
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shuo Liu, Shi-Xin Zhang, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Shengyu Zhang, Hong Yao. Non-equilibrium physics including many-body localization (MBL) has attracted increasing attentions, but theoretical approaches of reliably studying non-equilibrium properties remain quite limited. In this Letter, we propose a systematic approach to probe MBL phases via the excited-state variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and demonstrate convincing results of MBL on a quantum hardware, which we believe paves a promising way for future simulations of non-equilibrium systems beyond the reach of classical computations in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum

title: BASS XXIX: The near-infrared view of the BLR: the effects of obscuration in BLR characterisation Journal: ApJ This paper includes data gathered with the 6.5 meter Magellan Telescopes located at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile. Facilities: Magellan-LCO, Swift (BAT) FireHose (v2; Gagne et al. 2015), m

Koss, Jakob S. den Brok, Mislav Baloković, Rudolf Bär, Patricia Bessiere, Turgay Caglar, Fiona Harrison, Kohei Ichikawa, Darshan Kakkad, Isabella Lamperti, Richard Mushotzky, Kyuseok Oh, Meredith C. Powell, Georg
description: Abstract Virial black hole mass ( M B ​ H M_{BH} ) determination directly involves knowing the broad line region (BLR) clouds velocity distribution, their distance from the central supermassive black hole ( R B ​ L ​ R R_{BLR} ) and the virial factor ( f f ).

title: Neutrino flavor mixing with moments
creator: McKenzie Myers, Theo Cooper, MacKenzie Warren, Jim Kneller, Gail McLaughlin, Sherwood Richers, Evan Grohs, Carla Fröhlich
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by McKenzie Myers, Theo Cooper, MacKenzie Warren, Jim Kneller, Gail McLaughlin, Sherwood Richers, Evan Grohs, Carla Fröhlich. The successful transition from core-collapse supernova simulations using classical neutrino transport to simulations using quantum neutrino transport will require the development of methods for calculating neutrino flavor transformations that mitigate the computational expense. One potential approach is the use of angular moments of the neutrino field, which has the added appeal that there already exist simulation codes which make use of moments for classical neutrino transport.

title: Enforcing and Discovering Structure in Machine Learning
creator: Francesco Locatello
description: Abstract \dissnum 27248 \acatitle MSc ETH in Computer Science, ETH Zurich \dateofbirth 01.08.1992 \citizen Italy \Year 2020 \examiners Prof. Dr. Gunnar Rätsch (ETH Zurich), examinerProf. Dr. Andreas Krause (ETH Zurich), co-examiner Prof. Dr. Bernhard Schölkopf (MPI Tübingen), co-examiner Prof. Dr. Volkan Cevher (EPFL), co-examiner \support \disclaimer Abstract The world is structured in countless ways.

title: SARS-CoV-2 dissemination using a network of the United States counties Thanks: Ruriko Yoshida is supported partially from NSF Statistics Program DMS 1916037.
creator: Patrick Urrutia, David Wren, Chrysafis Vogiatzis, Ruriko Yoshida
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Patrick Urrutia, David Wren, Chrysafis Vogiatzis, Ruriko Yoshida. During 2020 and 2021, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) transmission has been increasing amongst the world’s population at an alarming rate. Reducing the spread of SARS-CoV-2 and other diseases that are spread in similar manners is paramount for public health officials as they seek to effectively manage resources and potential population control measures such as social distancing and quarantines.

title: Flavour alignment of New Physics
creator: in light of the
description: Abstract We investigate the flavour alignment conditions that New Physics (NP) models need to satisfy in order to address the ( g − 2 ) μ (g-2)_{\mu} anomaly and, at the same time, be consistent with the tight bounds from μ → e ​ γ \mu\to e\gamma and τ → μ ​ γ \tau\to\mu\gamma .

title: Why interference phenomena do not capture the essence of quantum theory
creator: Lorenzo Catani, Matthew Leifer, David Schmid, Robert W. Spekkens
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Catani, Matthew Leifer, David Schmid, Robert W. Spekkens. Quantum interference phenomena are widely viewed as posing a challenge to the classical worldview. Feynman even went so far as to proclaim that they are the only mystery and the basic peculiarity of quantum mechanics.

title: Mapping Surface Code to Superconducting Quantum Processors
creator: Anbang Wu, Gushu Li, Hezi Zhang, Gian Giacomo Guerreschi, Yufei Ding, Yuan Xie
description: Abstract In this paper, we formally describe the three challenges of mapping surface code on superconducting devices, and present a comprehensive synthesis framework to overcome these challenges. The proposed framework consists of three optimizations. First, we adopt a geometrical method to allocate data qubits which ensures the existence of shallow syndrome extraction circuit.

title: Towards Efficient Ansatz Architecture for Variational Quantum Algorithms
creator: Anbang Wu, Gushu Li, Yuke Wang, Boyuan Feng, Yufei Ding, Yuan Xie
description: Abstract Variational quantum algorithms are the quantum analogy of the successful neural network in classical machine learning. The ansatz architecture design, which is similar to classical neural network architecture design, is critical to the performance of a variational quantum algorithm.

title: QECV : A Verification Framework for Quantum Error Correction Codes
creator: Anbang Wu, Gushu Li, Hezi Zhang, Gian Giacomo Guerreschi, Yuan Xie, Yufei Ding
description: Abstract Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is essential for the functioning of large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers, and its implementation is a very sophisticated process involving both quantum and classical hardware. Formulating and verifying the decomposition of logical operations into physical ones is a challenge in itself.

title: Equivariant analytical mapping of first principles Hamiltonians to accurate and transferable materials models
creator: Liwei Zhang, Berk Onat, Geneviève Dusson, Adam McSloy, G. Anand, Reinhard J. Maurer, Christoph Ortner, James R. Kermode
description: Abstract We propose a scheme to construct predictive models for Hamiltonian matrices in atomic orbital representation from ab initio data as a function of atomic and bond environments. The scheme goes beyond conventional tight binding descriptions as it represents the ab initio model to full order, rather than in two-centre or three-centre approximations.

title: Splitting rates in QCD plasmas from a non-perturbative determination of the momentum broadening kernel C ⁡ ( q ⟂ ) C(q_{\perp})
creator: Sören Schlichting, Ismail Soudi
description: Abstract We exploit a recent non-perturbative determination of the momentum broadening kernel C ⁡ ( b ⊥ ) C(b_{\bot}) in impact parameter space Moore et al. 2021 , to determine the momentum space broadening kernel C ⁡ ( q ⊥ ) C(q_{\bot}) in high-temperature QCD plasmas.

title: The protoplanetary disc around HD 169142: circumstellar or circumbinary? The protoplanetary disc around HD 169142: circumstellar or circumbinary? – 7 2020
creator: P. P. Poblete, N. Cuello, S. Pérez, S. Marino,, J. Calcino, E. Macías, Á. Ribas, A. Zurlo, J. Cuadra, M. Montesinos, S. Zúñiga-Fernández, A. Bayo, C. Pinte, F. Ménard , and D. J. Price
description: Abstract Stellar binaries represent a substantial fraction of stellar systems, especially among young stellar objects. Accordingly, binaries play an important role in setting the architecture of a large number of protoplanetary discs. Binaries in coplanar and polar orientations with respect to the circumbinary disc are stable configurations and could induce non-axisymmetric structures in the dust and gas distributions.

title: Variable resolution Poisson-disk sampling for meshing discrete fracture networks Journal: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
creator: Johannes Krotz, Matthew R. Sweeney, Carl W. Gable, Jeffrey D. Hyman, Juan M. Restrepo
description: Abstract We present the near-Maximal Algorithm for Poisson-disk Sampling (nMAPS) to generate point distributions for variable resolution Delaunay triangular and tetrahedral meshes in two and three-dimensions, respectively. nMAPS consists of two principal stages. In the first stage, an initial point distribution is produced using a cell-based rejection algorithm.

title: The dimensional evolution of structure and dynamics in hard sphere liquids
creator: Patrick Charbonneau, Yi Hu, Joyjit Kundu, Peter K. Morse
description: Abstract The formulation of the mean-field, infinite-dimensional solution of hard sphere glasses is a significant milestone for theoretical physics. How relevant this description might be for understanding low-dimensional glass-forming liquids, however, remains unclear. These liquids indeed exhibit a complex interplay between structure and dynamics, and the importance of this interplay might only slowly diminish as dimension d d increases.

title: Combinatorial Relationship Between Finite Fields and Fixed Points of Functions Going Up and Down
creator: Emerson León, Julián Pulido
description: Abstract We explore a combinatorial bijection between two seemingly unrelated topics: the roots of irreducible polynomials of degree m m over a finite field 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} for a prime number p p and the number of points that are periodic of order m m for a continuous piece-wise linear function g p : [ 0 , 1 ] →

title: On the inverse semigroup of bimodules over a C ∗ C^{*} -algebra Thanks: The research was supported by RSF (project No. 21-11-00080).
creator: V. Manuilov
description: Abstract . It was noticed recently that, given a metric space ( X , d X ) (X,d_{X}) , the equivalence classes of metrics on the disjoint union of the two copies of X X coinciding with d X d_{X} on each copy form an inverse semigroup M ⁡ ( X ) M(X) with respect to concatenation of metrics.

title: Toward Next Generation Open Radio Access Networks—What O-RAN Can and Cannot Do!
creator: 1 Aly S. Abdalla, 2 Pratheek S. Upadhyaya, 3 Vijay K. Shah and 1 Vuk Marojevic
description: Abstract The open radio access network (O-RAN) describes an industry-driven open architecture and interfaces for building next generation RANs with artificial intelligence (AI) controllers. We circulated a survey among researchers, developers, and practitioners to gather their perspectives on O-RAN as a framework for 6G wireless research and development (R&D).

title: Some examples of nonassociative coalgebras and supercoalgebras
description: Abstract . Locally finiteness of some varieties of nonassociative coalgebras is studied and the Gelfand-Dorfman construction for Novikov coalgebras and the Kantor construction for Jordan super-coalgebras are given. We give examples of a non-locally finite differential coalgebra, Novikov coalgebra, Lie coalgebra, Jordan super-coalgebra, and right-alternative coalgebra. The dual algebra of each of these examples satisfies very strong additional identities.

title: Triple Hill’s Vortex Synthetic Eddy Method
creator: John S. Haywood, Adrian Sescu, Shanti Bhushan, Chris Kees
description: Abstract The generation of initial or inflow synthetic turbulent velocity or scalar fields reproducing statistical characteristics of realistic turbulence is still a challenge. The synthetic eddy method, previously introduced in the context of inflow conditions for large eddy simulations, is based on the assumption that turbulence can be regarded as a superposition of coherent structures.

title: Groupoid Actions on Sets, Duality and a Morita Context
creator: Saradia Della Flora, Daiana Flôres, Andrea Morgado, Thaísa Tamusiunas
description: Abstract . Let 𝒢 \mathcal{G} and 𝒦 \mathcal{K} be groupoids. We present the notion of a ( 𝒢 α , 𝒦 β ) (\mathcal{G}_{\alpha},\mathcal{K}_{\beta}) -set and we prove a duality theorem in this context, which extends the duality theorem for graded algebras by groups obtained in [ 5 ] .

title: A Fast Evolutionary adaptation for MCTS in Pommerman
creator: Harsh Panwar, Saswata Chatterjee, Wil Dube
description: Abstract Artificial Intelligence, when amalgamated with games makes the ideal structure for research and advancing the field. Multi-agent games have multiple controls for each agent which generates huge amounts of data while increasing search complexity. Thus, we need advanced search methods to find a solution and create an artificially intelligent agent.

creator: Purevdorj Tuvaandorj
description: Abstract This paper develops permutation versions of identification-robust tests in linear instrumental variables regression. Unlike the existing randomization and rank-based tests in which independence between the instruments and the error terms is assumed, the permutation Anderson-Rubin (AR), Lagrange Multiplier (LM) and Conditional Likelihood Ratio (CLR) tests are asymptotically similar and robust to conditional heteroskedasticity under standard exclusion restriction i.e.

title: Programmatic Innovations that Accord with the Retention of Women in STEM Careers
creator: Rama Balasubramanian 1,3 , Danielle Findley-Van Nostrand 2 and Matthew C. Fleenor 1,4∗
description: Abstract Gender representation in the physical sciences remains inequitable and continues to lag behind other fields. Even though there exists adequate documentation regarding programmatic postures, difficulties persist within the physics discipline. In this paper, we present innovative, programmatic elements over an eight-year period at an undergraduate, liberal arts, physics program.

title: Online Causal Inference with Application to Near Real-Time Post-Market Vaccine Safety Surveillance
creator: Xu Shi and Lan Luo
description: Abstract Streaming data routinely generated by mobile phones, social networks, e-commerce, and electronic health records present new opportunities for near real-time surveillance of the impact of an intervention on an outcome of interest via causal inference methods. However, as data grow rapidly in volume and velocity, storing and combing data become increasingly challenging.

title: Towards Terabit LiFi Networking
creator: Ahmad Adnan Qidan, Taisir El-Gorashi1, Jaafar M. H. Elmirghani School of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, University of Leeds, LS2 9JT, United Kingdom Email: { a.a.qidan, t.e.h.elgorashi, j.m.h.elmirghani } @leeds.ac.uk
description: Abstract Light Fidelity (Li-Fi) is a networked version of optical wireless communication (OWC), which is a strong candidate to fulfill the unprecedented increase in user-traffic expected in the near future. In OWC, a high number of optical access points (APs) is usually deployed on the ceiling of an indoor environment to serve multiple users with different demands.

title: Learning from learning machines: a new generation of AI technology to meet the needs of science
creator: Luca Pion-Tonachini, Kristofer Bouchard, Hector Garcia Martin, Sean Peisert, W. Bradley Holtz, Anil Aswani, Dipankar Dwivedi, Haruko Wainwright, Ghanshyam Pilania, Benjamin Nachman, Babetta L. Marrone, Nicola Falco, Prabhat, Daniel Arnold, Alejandro Wolf-Yadlin, Sarah Powers, Sharlee Climer, Quinn J
description: Abstract We outline emerging opportunities and challenges to enhance the utility of AI for scientific discovery. The distinct goals of AI for industry versus the goals of AI for science create tension between identifying patterns in data versus discovering patterns in the world from data.

title: Exploring Lossy Compressibility through Statistical Correlations of Scientific Datasets
creator: David Krasowska 1 , Julie Bessac 2 , Robert Underwood 1 , Jon C. Calhoun 1 , Sheng Di 2 , and Franck Cappello 2
description: Abstract Lossy compression plays a growing role in scientific simulations where the cost of storing their output data can span terabytes. Using error bounded lossy compression reduces the amount of storage for each simulation; however, there is no known bound for the upper limit on lossy compressibility.

title: Preparation and fluorescent wavelength control of multi-color Nitrogen-doped carbon nano-dots
creator: Wenli Li, Ju Tang, Yuzhao Li, Han Bai, Weizuo Zhang, Jin Zhang*, Yiming Xiao*, Wen Xu *
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wenli Li, Ju Tang, Yuzhao Li, Han Bai, Weizuo Zhang, Jin Zhang*, Yiming Xiao*, Wen Xu *. It is known that, by taking advantage of heteroatom doping, the electronic states and transition channels in carbon nano-dots (CNDs) can be effectively modulated. Thus, the photoluminescence (PL) properties of CNDs can be changed. For potential applications of CNDs as advanced materials for optoelectronic devices, it is important and significant to develop the practical techniques for doping heteroatoms into CNDs.

title: The PAT model of population dynamics
creator: Z. C. Feng, Y. Charles Li
description: Abstract . We introduce a population-age-time (PAT) model which describes the temporal evolution of the population distribution in age. The surprising result is that the qualitative nature of the population distribution dynamics is robust with respect to the birth rate and death rate distributions in age, and initial conditions.

title: Lafite : Towards Language-Free Training for Text-to-Image Generation
creator: Yufan Zhou, Ruiyi Zhang, Changyou Chen, Chunyuan Li, Chris Tensmeyer, Tong Yu, Jiuxiang Gu, Jinhui Xu, Tong Sun
description: Abstract One of the major challenges in training text-to-image generation models is the need of a large number of high-quality image-text pairs. While image samples are often easily accessible, the associated text descriptions typically require careful human captioning, which is particularly time- and cost-consuming.

title: Factorized Fourier Neural Operators
creator: Alasdair Tran, Alexander Mathews, Lexing Xie, Cheng Soon Ong
description: Abstract We propose the Factorized Fourier Neural Operator, a learning-based approach for simulating partial differential equations (PDEs). Starting from a recently proposed Fourier representation of flow fields, the Factorized Fourier Neural Operator bridges the performance gap between pure machine learning approaches to that of the best numerical or hybrid solvers.

title: New evidence for wet accretion of inner solar system planetesimals from meteorites Chelyabinsk and Benenitra Journal: PSJ
creator: Ziliang Jin, Maitrayee Bose, Tim Lichtenberg, Gijs D. Mulders
description: Abstract We investigated the hydrogen isotopic compositions and water contents of pyroxenes in two recent ordinary chondrite falls, namely, Chelyabinsk (2013 fall) and Benenitra (2018 fall), and compared them to three ordinary chondrite Antarctic finds, namely Graves Nunataks GRA 06179, Larkman Nunatak LAR 12241, and Dominion Range DOM 10035.

title: Multiple Equilibrium States of the Loop Current in the Gulf of Mexico Journal: jpo
description: Abstract It is known that western boundary currents, which encounter a gap in their supporting boundary, assume two dominant steady states: a loop current state and a gap leaping state, and that transitions between these states display hysteresis. However, a question of whether the idealized geometries considered to date apply to the Gulf of Mexico Loop Current (LC) remained.

title: Lensing Without Borders. I. A Blind Comparison of the Amplitude of Galaxy-Galaxy Lensing Between Independent Imaging Surveys
creator: A. Leauthaud, A. Amon, S. Singh, D. Gruen, J. U. Lange, S. Huang, N. C. Robertson, T. N. Varga, Y. Luo, C. Heymans, H. Hildebrandt, C. Blake, M. Aguena, S. Allam, F. Andrade-Oliveira, J. Annis, E. Bertin, S. Bhargava, J. Blazek, S. L. Bridle, D. Brooks, D. L. Burke, A. Carnero Rosell, M. Carrasco Ki
description: Abstract Lensing Without Borders is a cross-survey collaboration created to assess the consistency of galaxy-galaxy lensing signals ( Δ ​ Σ \Delta\Sigma ) across different data-sets and to carry out end-to-end tests of systematic errors. We perform a blind comparison of the amplitude of Δ ​ Σ \Delta\Sigma using lens samples from BOSS and six independent lensing surveys.

title: Enumerations of Universal Cycles for k k -Permutations
creator: Zuling Chang, Jie Xue
description: Abstract Universal cycle for k k -permutations is a cyclic arrangement in which each k k -permutation appears exactly once as k k consecutive elements. Enumeration problem of universal cycles for k k -permutations is discussed and one new enumerating method is proposed in this paper. Accurate enumerating formulae are provided when k = 2 , 3 k=2,3 .

title: Offline Neural Contextual Bandits: Pessimism, Optimization and Generalization
creator: Thanh Nguyen-Tang, Sunil Gupta, A.Tuan Nguyen, Svetha Venkatesh
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Thanh Nguyen-Tang, Sunil Gupta, A.Tuan Nguyen, Svetha Venkatesh. Offline policy learning (OPL) leverages existing data collected a priori for policy optimization without any active exploration. Despite the prevalence and recent interest in this problem, its theoretical and algorithmic foundations in function approximation settings remain under-developed. In this paper, we consider this problem on the axes of distributional shift, optimization, and generalization in offline contextual bandits with neural networks.

title: Predicted Λ ​ Λ ¯ \Lambda\bar{\Lambda} and Ξ − ​ Ξ ¯ + \Xi^{-}\bar{\Xi}^{+} decay modes of the charmoniumlike Y ⁡ ( 4230 ) Y(4230)
creator: Ri-Qing Qian 1,2, Qi Huang 4, Xiang Liu 1,2,3
description: Abstract In this work, we predict the light hadronic decay channels Y ⁡ ( 4230 ) → Λ ​ Λ ¯ Y(4230)\to\Lambda\bar{\Lambda} and Ξ − ​ Ξ ¯ + \Xi^{-}\bar{\Xi}^{+} when treating the Y ⁡ ( 4230 ) Y(4230) as a vector charmonium state.

title: Average Outward Flux Skeletons for Environment Mapping and Topology Matching Thanks: Disclaimer : Babak Samari and Gregory Dudek contributed to this article in their personal capacity as Ph.D. student and Professor at McGill University, respectively.
description: Abstract We consider how to directly extract a road map (also known as a topological representation) of an initially-unknown 2-dimensional environment via an online procedure that robustly computes a retraction of its boundaries. While such approaches are well known for their theoretical elegance, computing such representations in practice is complicated when the data is sparse and noisy.

title: A Convolutional Autoencoder-Based Pipeline for Anomaly Detection and Classification of Periodic Variables
creator: Ho-Sang, Chan, Siu-Hei, Cheung, V. Ashley Villar, Shirley Ho
description: Abstract The periodic pulsations of stars teach us about their underlying physical process. We present a convolutional autoencoder-based pipeline as an automatic approach to search for out-of-distribution anomalous periodic variables within The Zwicky Transient Facility Catalog of Periodic Variable Stars (ZTF CPVS). We use an isolation forest to rank each periodic variable by its anomaly score.

title: How the Galaxy Stellar Spins Acquire a Peculiar Tidal Connection?
creator: Jounghun Lee, Jun-Sung Moon, Suk-Jin Yoon
description: Abstract We explore how the galaxy stellar spins acquire a peculiar tendency of being aligned with the major principal axes of the local tidal fields, in contrast to their DM counterparts which tend to be perpendicular to them, regardless of their masses.

title: Federated Deep Learning in Electricity Forecasting: An MCDM Approach
creator: Marco Repetto, Davide La Torre, Muhammad Tariq
description: Abstract Large-scale data analysis is growing at an exponential rate as data proliferates in our societies. This abundance of data has the advantage of allowing the decision-maker to implement complex models in scenarios that were prohibitive before. At the same time, such an amount of data requires a distributed thinking approach.

title: Partner Personas Generation for Diverse Dialogue Generation
creator: Hongyuan Lu, Wai Lam, Hong Cheng, Helen M. Meng
description: Abstract Incorporating personas information allows diverse and engaging responses in dialogue response generation. Unfortunately, prior works have primarily focused on self personas and have overlooked the value of partner personas. Moreover, in practical applications, the availability of ground truth partner personas is often not the case.

title: Antiferromagnetism and large magnetoresistance in GdBi single crystal
creator: Gourav Dwari, Souvik Sasmal, Bishal Maity, Vikas Saini, Ruta Kulkarni, Arumugam Thamizhavel
description: Abstract Single crystal of the binary equi-atomic compound GdBi crystallizing in the rock salt type cubic crystal structure with the space group F ​ m ​ 3 ¯ ​ m Fm\bar{3}m has been grown by flux method. The electrical and magnetic measurements have been performed on well oriented single crystals.

title: Signatures of linear Breit-Wheeler pair production in polarized γ ​ γ \gamma\gamma collisions
creator: Qian Zhao, Liang Tang, Feng Wan, Bo-Chao Liu, Ruo-Yu Liu, Rui-Zhi Yang, Jin-Qing Yu, Xue-Guang Ren, Zhong-Feng Xu, Yong-Tao Zhao, Yong-Sheng Huang, Jian-Xing Li
description: Abstract Laser-driven brilliant controllable polarized γ \gamma -photon sources open the way for designing compact γ ​ γ \gamma\gamma collider, which enable the large yield of linear Breit-Wheeler (LBW) pairs in a single shot and thus provide an opportunity for the investigation of polarized LBW process.

title: DSC: Deep Scan Context Descriptor for Large-Scale Place Recognition
creator: Jiafeng Cui, Tengfei Huang, Yingfeng Cai, Junqiao Zhao, Lu Xiong, Zhuoping Yu
description: Abstract LiDAR-based place recognition is an essential and challenging task both in loop closure detection and global relocalization. We propose Deep Scan Context (DSC), a general and discriminative global descriptor that captures the relationship among segments of a point cloud.

title: Resource Allocation for IRS-Enabled Secure Multiuser Multi-Carrier Downlink URLLC Systems
creator: Mohammad Naseri Tehrani, Friedrich-Alexander-University (FAU), Erlangen-Nuremberg, Germany. email: moh.naseritehrani@fau.de, Shahrokh Farahmand
description: Abstract Secure ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) has been recently investigated with the fundamental limits of finite block length (FBL) regime in mind. Analysis has revealed that when eavesdroppers outnumber BS antennas or enjoy a more favorable channel condition compared to the legitimate users, base station (BS) transmit power should increase exorbitantly to meet quality of service (QoS) constraints.

title: Analogue Radio Over Fiber for Next-Generation RAN: Challenges and Opportunities
creator: Yichuan Li, Qijie Xie, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Senior Member, IEEE , Lajos Hanzo, Fellow, IEEE
description: Abstract The radio access network (RAN) connects the users to the core networks, where typically digitised radio over fiber (D-RoF) links are employed. The data rate of the RAN is limited by the hardware constraints of the D-RoF-based backhaul and fronthaul.

title: CATEGORY THEORY WITH EXAMPLES IN PROBABILITY THEORY
creator: WILLIAM GABRIEL GRANDA BETANCOURT
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by WILLIAM GABRIEL GRANDA BETANCOURT. Abstract The basic concepts of category theory are developed and examples of them are presented to illustrate them using measurement theory and probability theory tools. Motivated by Perrone’s work [ 4 ] where notes on category theory are developed with examples of basic mathematics, we present the concepts of category, functor, natural transformation, and products with examples in the probabilistic context.

title: Analogue Radio over Fiber aided Multi-service Communications for High Speed Trains
creator: Yichuan Li, Salman Ghafoor, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Senior Member, IEEE
description: Abstract High speed trains (HST) have gradually become an essential means of transportation, where given our digital world, it is expected that passengers will be connected all the time. More specifically, the on-board passengers require fast mobile connections, which cannot be provided by the currently implemented cellular networks.

title: Benchmarks for quantum computers from Shor’s algorithm
creator: E. D. Davis
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by E. D. Davis. Properties of Shor’s algorithm and the related period-finding algorithm could serve as benchmarks for the operation of a quantum computer. Distinctive universal behaviour is expected for the probability for success of the period-finding algorithm as the input quantum register is increased through its critical size of 𝔪 0 = ⌈ 2 ​ log 2 ​ r ⌉ \mathfrak{m}_{0}=\lceil 2\log_{2}r\rceil qubits (where r r is the period sought).

title: Quantum Complementarity Approach to Device-Independent Security
creator: Xingjian Zhang 1, Pei Zeng 1, Tian Ye 1, Hoi-Kwong Lo 2, 3, 4, Xiongfeng Ma 1
description: Abstract Complementarity is an essential feature of quantum mechanics. The preparation of an eigenstate of one observable implies complete randomness in its complementary observable. In quantum cryptography, complementarity allows us to formulate security analyses in terms of phase-error correction. However, in the device-independent regime that offers security without device characterization, the concept becomes much subtler.

title: Asymptotic spectra of large (grid) graphs with a uniform local structure (part II): numerical applications
creator: Andrea Adriani, Davide Bianchi, Paola Ferrari, Stefano Serra-Capizzano
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Andrea Adriani, Davide Bianchi, Paola Ferrari, Stefano Serra-Capizzano. In the current work we are concerned with sequences of graphs having a grid geometry, with a uniform local structure in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ d \Omega\subset{\mathbb{R}}^{d} , d ≥ 1 d\geq 1 . When Ω = [ 0 , 1 ] \Omega=[0,1] , such graphs include the standard Toeplitz graphs and, for Ω = [ 0 , 1 ] d \Omega=[0,1]^{d} , the considered class includes d d -level Toeplitz graphs.

title: Why Mercury is a Superconductor
creator: Cesare Tresca, Gianni Profeta, Giovanni Marini, Giovanni B. Bachelet, Antonio Sanna, Matteo Calandra, Lilia Boeri
description: Abstract Despite being the oldest known superconductor, solid mercury is mysteriously absent from all current computational databases of superconductors. In this work, we present a critical study of its superconducting properties based on state-of-the-art superconducting density-functional theory. Our calculations reveal numerous anomalies in electronic and lattice properties, which can mostly be handled, with due care, by modern ab-initio techniques.

title: Efficient thermoelectricity in Sr 2 Nb 2 O 7 with energy-dependent relaxation times
creator: Giulio Casu, Andrea Bosin, Vincenzo Fiorentini
description: Abstract We evaluate theoretically the thermoelectric efficiency of the layered perovskite Sr 2 Nb 2 O 7 via calculations of the electronic structure and transport coefficients within density-functional theory and Bloch-Boltzmann relaxation-time transport theory. The predicted figure-of-merit tensor Z ​ T ZT , computed with energy-, chemical potential- and temperature-dependent relaxation times, has one component increasing monotonically from around 0.

title: Galactic H ii region IRAS 17149 − - 3916 - A multiwavelength study 2020 Galactic H ii region IRAS 17149 − - 3916 - A multiwavelength study – References
creator: Ajay Potdar, Swagat R Das, Namitha Issac, Anandmayee Tej, Sarita Vig, C. H. Ishwara Chandra
description: Abstract This paper presents a multiwavelength investigation of the Galactic H ii region IRAS 17149 − - 3916. Using the Giant Meterwave Radio Telescope, India, first low-frequency radio continuum observations at 610 and 1280 MHz for this region are presented. The ionized gas emission displays an interesting cometary morphology which is likely powered by the early type source, E4 (IRS-1).

title: Giant thermoelectric figure of merit in multivalley high-complexity-factor LaSO
creator: Roberta Farris, Francesco Ricci, Giulio Casu, Diana Dahliah, Geoffroy Hautier, Gian-Marco Rignanese, Vincenzo Fiorentini
description: Abstract We report a giant thermoelectric figure of merit Z ​ T ZT (up to 6 at 1100 K) in n n -doped lanthanum oxysulphate LaSO. Thermoelectric coefficients are computed from ab initio bands within Bloch-Boltzmann theory in an energy-, chemical potential- and temperature-dependent relaxation time approximation.

title: Normative Disagreement as a Challenge for Cooperative AI
creator: Julian Stastny, Maxime Riché, Alexander Lyzhov, Johannes Treutlein, Allan Dafoe, Jesse Clifton
description: Abstract Cooperation in settings where agents have both common and conflicting interests (mixed-motive environments) has recently received considerable attention in multi-agent learning. However, the mixed-motive environments typically studied have a single cooperative outcome on which all agents can agree. Many real-world multi-agent environments are instead bargaining problems (BPs): they have several Pareto-optimal payoff profiles over which agents have conflicting preferences.

title: Truncated Geometry on the Circle
creator: E. Hekkelman
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by E. Hekkelman. In this letter we prove that the pure state space on the n × n n\times n complex Toeplitz matrices converges in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense to the state space on C ⁡ ( S 1 ) C(S^{1}) as n n grows to infinity, if we equip these sets with the metrics defined by the Connes distance formula for their respective natural Dirac operators.

title: ML-based Handover Prediction and AP Selection in Cognitive Wi-Fi Networks
creator: Muhammad Asif Khan 1 , Ridha Hamila 2 , Adel Gastli 2 , Serkan Kiranyaz 2 and Nasser Ahmed Al-Emadi 2
description: Abstract Device mobility in dense Wi-Fi networks offers several challenges. Two well-known problems related to device mobility are handover prediction and access point selection. Due to the complex nature of the radio environment, analytical models may not characterize the wireless channel, which makes the solution of these problems very difficult.

title: Gravitational wave memory of the binary black hole events in GWTC-2
creator: Zhi-Chao Zhao, Xiaolin Liu, Zhoujian Cao, Xiaokai He
description: Abstract Gravitational wave (GW) memory is an important prediction of general relativity. Existing works on the GW memory detection focus on the waveform analysis. It is hard for waveform analysis method to detect the GW memory due to its quasi-direct current behavior and weakness. We implement a completely different scheme in this work to estimate the GW memory.

title: A dual semismooth Newton based augmented Lagrangian method for large-scale linearly constrained sparse group square-root Lasso problems
creator: Chengjing Wang, Peipei Tang
description: Abstract Square-root Lasso problems are proven robust regression problems. Furthermore, square-root regression problems with structured sparsity also plays an important role in statistics and machine learning. In this paper, we focus on the numerical computation of large-scale linearly constrained sparse group square-root Lasso problems.

title: Validity of Bogoliubov’s approximation for translation-invariant Bose gases
creator: Morris Brooks and Robert Seiringer
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Morris Brooks and Robert Seiringer. We verify Bogoliubov’s approximation for translation-invariant Bose gases in the mean field regime, i.e. we prove that the ground state energy E N E_{N} is given by E N = N ​ e H + inf σ ⁡ ( ℍ ) + o N → ∞ ​ ( 1 ) E_{N}=Ne_{\mathrm{H}}+\inf\sigma\left(\mathbb{H}\right)+o_{N\rightarrow\infty}(1) , where N N is the number of particles, e H e_{\mathrm{H}} is the minimal Hartree energy and ℍ \mathbb{H} is the Bogoliubov Hamiltonian.

title: Stochastic gravitational wave background due to gravitational wave memory
creator: Zhi-Chao Zhao, Zhoujian Cao
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zhi-Chao Zhao, Zhoujian Cao. Gravitational wave memory is an important prediction of general relativity, which has not been detected yet. Amounts of memory events can form a stochastic gravitational wave memory background. Here we find that memory background can be described as a Brownian motion in the condition that the observation time is longer than the averaged time interval between two successive memory events. We investigate, for the first time, the memory background of binary black hole coalescences.

title: Automated Antenna Testing Using Encoder-Decoder-based Anomaly Detection
creator: 1 st Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, 2 nd Jiawen Xu, 3 rd Ravi Sama, 4 th Matthias Kovatsch
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by 1 st Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, 2 nd Jiawen Xu, 3 rd Ravi Sama, 4 th Matthias Kovatsch. We propose a new method for testing antenna arrays that records the radiating electromagnetic (EM) field using an absorbing material and evaluating the resulting thermal image series through an AI using a conditional encoder-decoder model.
