creator: Yuhan Gan, Wei Xia ∗, Long Zhang ∗, Kunya Yang, Xinrun Mi, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Yanfeng Guo, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Mingquan He
description: Abstract We present a study of Seebeck and Nernst effect in combination with magnetoresistance and Hall measurements of the Kagome superconductor CsV 3 {}_{\mbox{3}} Sb 5 {}_{\mbox{5}} . Sizable magneto-Seebeck signal appears once the charge density wave (CDW) order sets in below T C ​ D ​ W T_{CDW} =94 K.

title: Machine learning aided noise filtration and signal classification for CREDO experiment
creator: Piotr Homola
description: Abstract The wealth of smartphone data collected by the Cosmic Ray Extremely Distributed Observatory (CREDO) greatly surpasses the capabilities of manual analysis. So, efficient means of rejecting the non-cosmic-ray noise and identification of signals attributable to extensive air showers are necessary.

title: Conditional wave theory of environmental interactions with a quantum particle
creator: Rory van Geleuken, Andrew V. Martin
description: Abstract We present an alternative formulation of quantum decoherence theory using conditional wave theory (CWT), which was originally developed in molecular physics (also known as exact factorisation methods). We formulate a CWT of a classic model of collisional decoherence of a free particle with environmental particles treated in a long-wavelength limit.

title: From SLAM to Situational Awareness: Challenges and Survey
creator: Hriday Bavle, Jose Luis Sanchez-Lopez, Claudio Cimarelli, Ali Tourani, Holger Voos
description: Abstract The capability of a mobile robot to efficiently and safely perform complex missions is limited by its knowledge of the environment, namely the situation . Advanced reasoning, decision-making, and execution skills enable an intelligent agent to act autonomously in unknown environments.

creator: Eric Bezzam, Sepand Kashani, Paul Hurley, Martin Vetterli, Matthieu Simeoni

However, many applications involve an underlying continuous signal, and a more natural choice would be to work with e.g.

title: Censored autoregressive regression models with Student- t t innovations
creator: Katherine A. L. Valeriano, Fernanda L. Schumacher, Christian E. Galarza, Larissa A. Matos
description: Abstract The Student- t t distribution is widely used in statistical modeling of datasets involving outliers since its longer-than-normal tails provide a robust approach to hand such data. Furthermore, data collected over time may contain censored or missing observations, making it impossible to use standard statistical procedures.

title: Integration in semirings
creator: Ivan Chajda, Helmut Länger
description: Abstract The concept of integral as an inverse to that of derivation was already introduced for rings and recently also for lattices. Since semirings generalize both rings and bounded distributive lattices, it is natural to investigate integration in semirings. This is our aim in the present paper.

title: Modulational Instabity of Spin-Orbit Coupled Bose-Einstein Condensates in Discrete Media Journal: Physics Letters A
creator: S. Sabari 1,∗ , R. TamilThiruvalluvar 2,† and R. Radha 1,#
description: Abstract We address the impact of intra-site spin-orbit (SO) coupling and associated inter-component Rabi coupling on the modulational instability (MI) of plane-wave states in two-component discrete Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). Conditions for the onset of the MI and the respective instability are found analytically.

title: gnlse-python : Open Source Software to Simulate Nonlinear Light Propagation In Optical Fibers
creator: Paweł Redman, Magdalena Zatorska, Adam Pawłowski, Daniel Szulc, Sylwia Majchrowska, Karol Tarnowski
description: Abstract The propagation of pulses in optical fibers is described by the generalized nonlinear Schrodinger equation (GNLSE), which takes into account the fiber losses, nonlinear effects, and higher-order chromatic dispersion. The GNLSE is a partial differential equation, whose order depends on the accounted nonlinear and dispersion effects.

title: SALSA: Spatial Cue-Augmented Log-Spectrogram Features for Polyphonic Sound Event Localization and Detection
creator: Thi Ngoc Tho Nguyen, Karn N. Watcharasupat, Ngoc Khanh Nguyen, Douglas L. Jones, Woon-Seng Gan
description: Abstract Sound event localization and detection (SELD) consists of two subtasks, which are sound event detection and direction-of-arrival estimation. While sound event detection mainly relies on time-frequency patterns to distinguish different sound classes, direction-of-arrival estimation uses amplitude and/or phase differences between microphones to estimate source directions. As a result, it is often difficult to jointly optimize these two subtasks.

creator: David Michael Roberts
description: Abstract This article re-examines Lawvere’s abstract, category-theoretic proof of the fixed-point theorem whose contrapositive is a ‘universal’ diagonal argument. The main result is that the necessary axioms for both the fixed-point theorem and the diagonal argument can be stripped back further, to a semantic analogue of a weak substructural logic lacking weakening or exchange. \homepage https://ncatlab.
