title: NaRLE: Natural Language Models using Reinforcement Learning with Emotion Feedback
creator: Ruijie Zhou, Soham Deshmukh, Jeremiah Greer, Charles Lee
description: Abstract Current research in dialogue systems is focused on conversational assistants working on short conversations in either task-oriented or open domain settings. In this paper, we focus on improving task-based conversational assistants online, primarily those working on document-type conversations (e.g., emails) whose contents may or may not be completely related to the assistant’s task.

title: Inference and De-Noising of Non-Gaussian Particle Distribution Functions: A Generative Modeling Approach Thanks: Partially Supported by Department of Energy Grant 17-SC-20-SC
creator: 1 st John Donaghy, 2 st Kai Germaschewski
description: Abstract The particle-in-cell numerical method of plasma physics balances a trade-off between computational cost and intrinsic noise. Inference on data produced by these simulations generally consists of binning the data to recover the particle distribution function, from which physical processes may be investigated.

title: Electrochemistry meets polymer physics: polymerized ionic liquids on an electrified electrode
creator: Yury A. Budkov, Nikolai N. Kalikin, Andrei L. Kolesnikov
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yury A. Budkov, Nikolai N. Kalikin, Andrei L. Kolesnikov. Polymeric ionic liquids are emerging polyelectrolyte materials for modern electrochemical applications. In this paper, we propose a self-consistent field theory of the polymeric ionic liquid on a charged conductive electrode.

title: Fast barrier-free switching in synthetic antiferromagnets
creator: Yu. Dzhezherya, V. Kalita, P. Polynchuk, A. Kravets, V. Korenivski, S. Kruchinin, S. Bellucci
description: Abstract We analytically solve the Landau-Lifshitz equations for the collective magnetization dynamics in a synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) nanoparticle and uncover a regime of barrier-free switching under a short small-amplitude magnetic field pulse applied perpendicular to the SAF plane. We give examples of specific implementations for forming such low-power and ultra-fast switching pulses.

title: Thermometry of Gaussian quantum systems using Gaussian measurements
creator: Marina F.B. Cenni, Ludovico Lami, Antonio Acín, Mohammad Mehboudi
description: Abstract We study the problem of estimating the temperature of Gaussian systems with feasible measurements, namely Gaussian and photo-detection-like measurements. For Gaussian measurements, we develop a general method to identify the optimal measurement numerically, and derive the analytical solutions in some relevant cases.

title: Wasserstein distance and metric trees
creator: Maxime MATHEY-PREVOT, Alain VALETTE
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Maxime MATHEY-PREVOT, Alain VALETTE. We study the Wasserstein (or earthmover) metric on the space P ⁡ ( X ) P(X) of probability measures on a metric space X X . We show that, if a finite metric space X X embeds stochastically with distortion D D in a family of finite metric trees, then P ⁡ ( X ) P(X) embeds bi-Lipschitz into ℓ 1 \ell^{1} with distortion D D .

title: A Community Roadmap for Scientific Workflows Research and Development
creator: Rafael Ferreira da Silva 1 2 , Henri Casanova 3 , Kyle Chard 4 5 , Ilkay Altintas 6 , Rosa M Badia 7 , Bartosz Balis 8 , Tainã Coleman 2 , Frederik Coppens 9 10 , Frank Di Natale 11 , Bjoern Enders 21 , Thomas Fahringer 12 , Rosa Filgueira 13 , Grigori Fursin 14 , Daniel Garijo 15 , Carole Goble 16
description: Abstract The landscape of workflow systems for scientific applications is notoriously convoluted with hundreds of seemingly equivalent workflow systems, many isolated research claims, and a steep learning curve. To address some of these challenges and lay the groundwork for transforming workflows research and development, the WorkflowsRI and ExaWorks projects partnered to bring the international workflows community together.

title: Online Application Guidance for Heterogeneous Memory Systems Note: Extension of Conference Paper: While not a true extension, this work builds upon prior contributions published at the IEEE International Conference on Networking, Architecture, and Storage ( Best Paper Award ) ( Olson et al. 2018 ) a
creator: M. Ben Olson, Brandon Kammerdiener, Kshitij A. Doshi, Terry Jones, Michael R. Jantz
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Ben Olson, Brandon Kammerdiener, Kshitij A. Doshi, Terry Jones, Michael R. Jantz. As scaling of conventional memory devices has stalled, many high end and next generation computing systems have begun to incorporate alternative memory technologies to meet performance goals. Since these technologies present distinct advantages and tradeoffs compared to conventional DDR* SDRAM, such as higher bandwidth with lower capacity or vice versa, they are typically packaged alongside conventional SDRAM in a heterogeneous memory architecture.

title: Derivative Extrapolation Using Least Squares
creator: Nick Butler, Ian Faber, Boris Shapoval, Armen Davis, Peter Borrell, Jake Mcgrath
description: Abstract Abstract Here, we present three methods for differentiating discrete sets from streaming processes, e.g. WIFI. One approach is based on optimization of the well-known Savitzky-Golay algorithm. These methods are tested on synthetic data sets and will be implemented on subsets of a real university campus WIFI data set.

title: Halos and undecidability of tensor stable positive maps
creator: Mirte van der Eyden, Tim Netzer, Gemma De las Cuevas
description: Abstract . A map 𝒫 \mathcal{P} is tensor stable positive (tsp) if 𝒫 ⊗ n \mathcal{P}^{\otimes n} is positive for all n n , and essential tsp if it is not completely positive or completely co-positive. Are there essential tsp maps? Here we prove that there exist essential tsp maps on the hypercomplex numbers.

title: Analysis and Optimization of HARQ for URLLC
creator: Faisal Nadeem, Yonghui Li, Branka Vucetic, Mahyar Shirvanimoghaddam
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Faisal Nadeem, Yonghui Li, Branka Vucetic, Mahyar Shirvanimoghaddam. In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of the hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) technique in providing high-reliability and low-latency in the finite blocklength (FBL) regime in a single user uplink scenario. We characterize the packet error rate (PER), throughput, and delay performance of chase combining HARQ (CC-HARQ) and incremental redundancy HARQ (IR-HARQ) in AWGN and Rayleigh fading channel with m m retransmissions.

title: New black hole solutions in three-dimensional f ⁡ ( R ) \mathit{f(R)} gravity
creator: G.G.L. Nashed, A. Sheykhi
description: Abstract We construct two new classes of analytical solutions in three-dimensional spacetime and in the framework of f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity. The first class represents a non-rotating black hole (BH) while the second class corresponds to a rotating BH solution.

title: Double Inozemtsev Limits of the Quantum DELL System
creator: Alexander Gorsky, Peter Koroteev, Olesya Koroteeva, Shamil Shakirov
description: Abstract . In this letter we study various Inozemtsev-type limits of the quantum double elliptic (DELL) system when both elliptic parameters are sent to zero at different rates, while the coupling constant is sent to infinity, such that a certain combination of the three parameters is kept fixed.

title: Essentially exact numerical modelling of flux qubit chains subject to charge and flux noise
creator: Matthew R.C. Fitzpatrick, Jack Raymond, Malcolm P. Kennett
description: Abstract We present an essentially exact numerical method for modelling flux qubit chains subject to charge and flux noise. We define an essentially exact method as one that introduces errors that are completely controlled such that they can be made arbitrarily small by tuning the simulation parameters.

title: Revealing a charge-density-wave gap in the predicted weak topological insulator HoSbTe
creator: J. L. Liu, R. Liu, M. Yang, L. Y. Cao, B. X. Gao, L. Wang, A. F. Fang, Y. G. Shi, Z. P. Yin, R. Y. Chen
description: Abstract HoSbTe was predicted to be a weak topological insulator, whose spin-orbit coupling (SOC) gaps are reported to be as large as hundreds of meV. Utilizing infrared spectroscopy, we find that the compound is of metallic nature from 350 K down to 10 K.

title: Two Disjoint Alternating Paths in Bipartite Graphs
creator: Archontia C. Giannopoulou – National and Kapodistrian University of Athens archontia.giannopoulou@gmail.com Sebastian Wiederrecht – LIRMM, University of Montpellier sebastian.wiederrecht@gmail.com
description: Abstract A bipartite graph B B is called a brace if it is connected and every matching of size at most two in B B is contained in some perfect matching of B B and A cycle C C in B B is called conformal if B − V ⁡ ( C ) B-V(C) has a perfect matching.

title: Novel constraints on neutrino physics beyond the standard model from the CONUS experiment CONUS Collaboration
creator: H. Bonet, A. Bonhomme, C. Buck, K. Fülber, J. Hakenmüller, G. Heusser, T. Hugle, M. Lindner, W. Maneschg, T. Rink, H. Strecker, and R. Wink
description: Abstract The measurements of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE ν \nu NS) experiments have opened up the possibility to constrain neutrino physics beyond the standard model of elementary particle physics. Furthermore, by considering neutrino-electron scattering in the keV-energy region, it is possible to set additional limits on new physics processes.

title: The W s , p W^{s,p} -boundedness of stationary wave operators for the Schrödinger operator with inverse-square potential
creator: Changxing Miao, Xiaoyan Su, Jiqiang Zheng
description: Abstract . In this paper, we investigate the W s , p W^{s,p} -boundedness for stationary wave operators of the Schrödinger operator with inverse-square potential ℒ a = − Δ + a | x | 2 , a ≥ − ( d − 2 ) 2 4 , \mathcal{L}_{a}=-\Delta+\tfrac{a}{|x|^{2}},\quad a\geq-\tfrac{(d-2)^{2}}{4}, in dimension d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 .

title: Magnetic Structure and Propagation of Two Interacting CMEs from the Sun to Saturn
description: Abstract One of the grand challenges in heliophysics is the characterisation of coronal mass ejection (CME) magnetic structure and evolution from eruption at the Sun through heliospheric propagation. At present, the main difficulties are related to the lack of direct measurements of the coronal magnetic fields and the lack of 3D in-situ measurements of the CME body in interplanetary space.

title: Predicting Credit Risk for Unsecured Lending: A Machine Learning Approach
creator: K.S. Naik
description: Abstract Since the 1990s, there have been significant advances in the technology space and the e-Commerce area, leading to an exponential increase in demand for cashless payment solutions. This has led to increased demand for credit cards, bringing along with it the possibility of higher credit defaults and hence higher delinquency rates, over a period of time.

title: Secure Aggregation for Buffered Asynchronous Federated Learning
creator: Jinhyun So, Ramy E. Ali, Başak Güler, A. Salman Avestimehr
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jinhyun So, Ramy E. Ali, Başak Güler, A. Salman Avestimehr. Federated learning (FL) typically relies on synchronous training, which is slow due to stragglers. While asynchronous training handles stragglers efficiently, it does not ensure privacy due to the incompatibility with the secure aggregation protocols. A buffered asynchronous training protocol known as FedBuff has been proposed recently which bridges the gap between synchronous and asynchronous training to mitigate stragglers and to also ensure privacy simultaneously.

title: Photonic Topological Transitions and Epsilon-Near-Zero Surface Plasmons in Type-II Dirac Semimetal NiTe 2
creator: Carlo Rizza, Debasis Dutta, Barun Ghosh, Francesca Alessandro, Chia-Nung Kuo, Chin Shan Lue, Lorenzo S. Caputi, Arun Bansil, Amit Agarwal, Antonio Politano, Anna Cupolillo
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Carlo Rizza, Debasis Dutta, Barun Ghosh, Francesca Alessandro, Chia-Nung Kuo, Chin Shan Lue, Lorenzo S. Caputi, Arun Bansil, Amit Agarwal, Antonio Politano, Anna Cupolillo. Compared to artificial metamaterials, where nano-fabrication complexities and finite-size inclusions can hamper the desired electromagnetic response, several natural materials like van der Waals crystals hold great promise for designing efficient nanophotonic devices in the optical range.

title: Uncertainty Principles for Quaternion
creator: Linear Canonical S-Transform
description: Abstract Department of Mathematical Sciences, Islamic University of Science and Technology Awantipora, Pulwama, Jammu and Kashmir 192122, India. 1 gyounusg@gmail.com and 2 ahdkul740@gmail.com Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of quaternion linear canonical S-transform(Q-LCST) which is an extension of the linear canonical S-transform.

title: Rédei permutations with the same cycle structure Thanks: The second author received support for this project provided by a PSC-CUNY grant, jointly funded by The Professional Staff Congress and The City University of New York.
creator: Juliane Capaverde, Ariane M. Masuda, and Virgínia M. Rodrigues
description: Abstract . Let 𝔽 q \mathbb{F}_{q} be the finite field of order q q , and ℙ 1 ​ ( 𝔽 q ) = 𝔽 q ∪ { ∞ } \mathbb{P}^{1}(\mathbb{F}_{q})=\mathbb{F}_{q}\cup\{\infty\} . Write ( x + y ) m (x+\sqrt{y})^{m} as N ⁡ ( x , y ) + D ⁡ ( x , y ) ​ y N(x,y)+D(x,y)\sqrt{y} .

title: Label differential privacy via clustering
creator: Hossein Esfandiari, Vahab Mirrokni, Umar Syed, Sergei Vassilvitskii
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hossein Esfandiari, Vahab Mirrokni, Umar Syed, Sergei Vassilvitskii. We present new mechanisms for label differential privacy , a relaxation of differentially private machine learning that only protects the privacy of the labels in the training set. Our mechanisms cluster the examples in the training set using their (non-private) feature vectors, randomly re-sample each label from examples in the same cluster, and output a training set with noisy labels as well as a modified version of the true loss function.

title: A Semantic Model for Interacting Cyber-Physical Systems
creator: Benjamin Lion, Farhad Arbab, Carolyn Talcott
description: Abstract We propose a component-based semantic model for Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) wherein the notion of a component abstracts the internal details of both cyber and physical processes, to expose a uniform semantic model of their externally observable behaviors expressed as sets of sequences of observations. We introduce algebraic operations on such sequences to model different kinds of component composition.

title: Remarks on sparseness and regularity of Navier–Stokes solutions
creator: Dallas Albritton, Zachary Bradshaw
description: Abstract . The goal of this paper is twofold. First, we give a simple proof that sufficiently sparse Navier–Stokes solutions do not develop singularities. This provides an alternative to the approach of [ Gru13 ] , which is based on analyticity and the ‘harmonic measure maximum principle’.

title: Δ \Delta -UQ: Accurate Uncertainty Quantification via Anchor Marginalization
creator: Rushil Anirudh, Jayaraman J. Thiagarajan
description: Abstract We present Δ \Delta -UQ – a novel, general-purpose uncertainty estimator using the concept of anchoring in predictive models. Anchoring works by first transforming the input into a tuple consisting of an anchor point drawn from a prior distribution, and a combination of the input sample with the anchor using a pretext encoding scheme.

title: Anomalies and phases of strongly-coupled chiral gauge theories: recent developments
creator: Stefano Bolognesi, Kenichi Konishi, Andrea Luzio, [13pt] Department of Physics ”E. Fermi”, University of Pisa, [-5pt] Largo Pontecorvo, 3, Ed. C, 56127 Pisa, Italy, [2pt] INFN, Sezione di Pisa, Largo Pontecorvo, 3, Ed. C, 56127 Pisa, Italy, [2pt] Scuola Normale Superiore, Piazza dei Cavalieri, 7, 56
description: Abstract After many years of investigations, our understanding of the dynamics of strongly-coupled chiral gauge theories is still quite unsatisfactory today. Conventional wisdom about strongly-coupled gauge theories, successfully applied to QCD, is not always as useful in chiral gauge theories.

title: Upper bound on the rate of convergence and truncation bound for non-homogeneous birth and death processes on ℤ \mathbb{Z}
creator: Y. A. Satin, R. V. Razumchik, A. I. Zeifman, I. A. Kovalev
description: Abstract Abstract We consider the well-known problem of the computation of the (limiting) time-dependent performance characteristics of one-dimensional continuous-time birth and death processes on \mathbb{Z} with time varying and possible state-dependent intensities. First in the literature upper bounds on the rate of convergence along with one new concentration inequality are provided.

title: Efficient Modelling Across Time of Human Actions and Interactions
creator: Alexandros Stergiou, Alexandros Stergiou
description: Abstract \department Department \faculty Information and computing sciences \ISSN TBD \dissertationseries 1234 \uiotitle Chapter 0 Acknowledgements Four year ago I was accepted to work under the supervision of Ronald Poppe and Remco Veltkamp on dyadic human interactions. Over the course of these years, they have given me the opportunity to develop my own research ideas throughout my PhD.

title: Mix3D: Out-of-Context Data Augmentation for 3D Scenes
creator: Alexey Nekrasov Jonas Schult Or Litany Bastian Leibe Francis Engelmann
description: Abstract We present Mix3D, a data augmentation technique for segmenting large-scale 3D scenes. Since scene context helps reasoning about object semantics, current works focus on models with large capacity and receptive fields that can fully capture the global context of an input 3D scene.

title: Constraining baryonic feedback and cosmology with weak-lensing, X-ray, and kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich observations 2021 Constraining baryonic feedback and cosmology with weak-lensing, X-ray, and kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich observations – B
creator: Aurel Schneider, Sambit K. Giri, Stefania Amodeo, Alexandre Refregier
description: Abstract Modern weak-lensing observations are becoming increasingly sensitive to baryonic feedback processes which are still poorly understood. So far, this challenge has been faced either by imposing scale-cuts in the data or by modelling baryonic effects with simple, one-parameter models.

title: Acoustic spin and orbital angular momentum using evanescent Bessel beams
creator: Irving Rondón
description: Abstract Using acoustic evanescent Bessel beam is analyzed the fundamental properties for the spin and orbital angular momentum. The calculation shows that the transversal spin, the canonical momentum, and the orbital angular momentum are proportional to the ratio l / ω l/\omega , where l l is the topological charge and ω \omega the angular frequency.

title: Solving the membership problem for certain subgroups of S ​ L 2 ​ ( ℤ ) SL_{2}(\mathbb{Z}) Thanks: The second author received support for this project provided by a PSC-CUNY award, jointly funded by The Professional Staff Congress and The City University of New York.
creator: Sandie Han, Ariane M. Masuda, Satyanand Singh, and Johann Thiel
description: Abstract . For positive integers u u and v v , let L u = [ 1 0 u 1 ] L_{u}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\ u&1\end{bmatrix} and R v = [ 1 v 0 1 ] R_{v}=\begin{bmatrix}1&v\\ 0&1\end{bmatrix} . Let G u , v G_{u,v} be the group generated by L u L_{u} and R v R_{v} .

title: Jets in Common Envelopes: a low mass main sequence star in a red giant 2020 Jets in Common Envelopes: a low mass main sequence star in a red giant –
creator: Diego López-Cámara, Fabio De Colle, Enrique Moreno Méndez, Sagiv Shiber, Roberto Iaconi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Diego López-Cámara, Fabio De Colle, Enrique Moreno Méndez, Sagiv Shiber, Roberto Iaconi. We present small-scale three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of the evolution of a 0.3 M ⊙ M_{\odot} main sequence star which launches two perpendicular jets within the envelope of a 0.88 M ⊙ M_{\odot} red giant.

title: Discovery, TESS Characterization, and Modeling of Pulsations in the Extremely Low Mass White Dwarf GD 278 Journal: ApJ Facilities: Gaia , Struve, TESS IRAF ( Tody 1986 ) , barycorrpy ( Kanodia & Wright 2018 ) , lightkurve ( Lightkurve Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , Pyriod ( Bell 2020 ) , MESA ( Paxto
creator: Isaac D. Lopez, J. J. Hermes, Leila M. Calcaferro, Keaton J. Bell, Adam Samuels, Zachary P. Vanderbosch, Alejandro H. Córsico, Alina G. Istrate
description: Abstract We report the discovery of pulsations in the extremely low mass (ELM), likely helium-core white dwarf GD 278 via ground- and space-based photometry. GD 278 was observed by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) in Sector 18 at a 2-min cadence for roughly 24 d.

title: Classical Pendulum Clocks Break the Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
creator: Patrick Pietzonka
description: Abstract The thermodynamic uncertainty relation expresses a seemingly universal trade-off between the cost for driving an autonomous system and precision in any output observable. It has so far been proven for discrete systems and for overdamped Brownian motion. Its validity for the more general class of underdamped Brownian motion, where inertia is relevant, was conjectured based on numerical evidence.

title: Urns & Tubes
creator: Bart Jacobs
description: Abstract Urn models play an important role to express various basic ideas in probability theory. Here we extend this urn model with tubes. An urn contains coloured balls, which can be drawn with probabilities proportional to the numbers of balls of each colour. For each colour a tube is assumed. These tubes have different sizes (lengths).

title: Steady State in Ultrastrong Coupling Regime: Expansion and First Orders
creator: Camille Lombard Latune
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Camille Lombard Latune. U nderstanding better the dynamics and steady states of systems strongly coupled to thermal baths is a great theoretical challenge with promising applications in several fields of quantum technologies. Among several strategies to gain access to the steady state, one consists in obtaining approximate expressions of the mean force Gibbs state, the reduced state of the global system-bath thermal state, largely credited to be the steady state.

title: Thin-Walled Higgs Assisted Q-balls from Pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Bosons Preprint: OUTP-21-22P, DESY-21-155
creator: Fady Bishara, Olivier Lennon
description: Abstract We consider the question of whether Q-balls can exist in a chiral Lagrangian truncated at leading order when, in addition, the Standard Model Higgs boson couples to the pseudo-Nambu-Golstone bosons (pNGBs). In particular, we consider the so-called thin-wall limit where volume energy dominates over surface energy.

title: An Exploration of the Mentorship Needs of Research Software Engineers
creator: Reed Milewicz, Miranda Mundt
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Reed Milewicz, Miranda Mundt. As a newly designated professional title, research software engineers (RSEs) link the two worlds of software engineering and research science. They lack clear development and training opportunities, particularly in the realm of mentoring. In this paper, we discuss mentorship as it pertains to the unique needs of RSEs and propose ways in which organizations and institutions can support mentor/mentee relationships for RSEs.
